playamb

playamb - Ambisonics player

Python library and executable program to decode and play ambisonics files as binaural output. Additional features include a GUI and dynamic headtracking.

 2playamb - Ambisonics player

 4Python library and executable program to decode and play ambisonics files as binaural output. Additional features include a GUI and dynamic headtracking.

 25class AmbisonicsFile:
 26    """
 27    Memory-efficient Ambisonics audio loader.
 28
 29    Features:
 30    - TRUE chunked streaming
 31    - Low memory usage
 32    - float32 processing
 33    - pyfar compatibility
 34    """
 35
 36    _SUPPORTED_FORMATS = ("ambix", "fuma")
 37    _SUPPORTED_NORMALIZATIONS = ("SN3D", "N3D")
 38
 39    def __init__(
 40        self,
 41        filepath: str,
 42        chunk_size: int = 2048,
 43        order: Optional[int] = None,
 44        trim_extra_channels: bool = True,
 45        format: str = "ambix",
 46        normalization: str = "SN3D",
 47    ):
 48        """
 49        Open an Ambisonics WAV file for chunked streaming.
 50
 51        Parameters
 52        ----------
 53        filepath : str
 54            Path to the Ambisonics WAV file.
 55        chunk_size : int
 56            Number of samples per streaming chunk (clamped to [32, 8192],
 57            rounded up to the nearest power of two).  Default 2048.
 58        order : int or None
 59            Ambisonics order to decode.  When ``None`` (default), the order
 60            is auto-detected from the channel count via
 61            ``ambix_channels_to_order``.
 62        trim_extra_channels : bool
 63            When True (default), trailing channels beyond the expected
 64            ``(order+1)^2`` are discarded.  Set to False to keep all
 65            channels (may break decoding if extra channels are present).
 66        format : str
 67            Ambisonics format — ``"ambix"`` (ACN/SN3D, default) or
 68            ``"fuma"`` (WXY/Furse-Malham).
 69        normalization : str
 70            Channel normalisation — ``"SN3D"`` (default) or ``"N3D"``.
 71        """
 72
 73        if format not in self._SUPPORTED_FORMATS:
 74            raise ValueError(
 75                f"Unsupported format '{format}'. "
 76                f"Supported: {', '.join(self._SUPPORTED_FORMATS)}."
 77            )
 78        self.format = format
 79
 80        if normalization not in self._SUPPORTED_NORMALIZATIONS:
 81            raise ValueError(
 82                f"Unsupported normalization '{normalization}'. "
 83                f"Supported: {', '.join(self._SUPPORTED_NORMALIZATIONS)}."
 84            )
 85        self.normalization = normalization
 86
 87        self.filepath = filepath
 88        self.chunk_size = self._normalize_chunk_size(chunk_size)
 89
 90        # ==========================================================
 91        # Use soundfile for STREAMING instead of loading entire file
 92        # ==========================================================
 93
 94        self.file = sf.SoundFile(filepath)
 95
 96        self.samplerate = self.file.samplerate
 97        self.num_channels = self.file.channels
 98        self.total_frames = len(self.file)
 99
100        self.duration = self.total_frames / self.samplerate
101
102        # ==========================================================
103        # Validate AmbiX format
104        # ==========================================================
105
106        self._validate_ambix_format()
107
108        # ==========================================================
109        # Determine Ambisonics order
110        # ==========================================================
111
112        if order is not None:
113            self.order = order
114            logger.info("Using user-specified order: %d", self.order)
115        else:
116            self.order = ambix_channels_to_order(self.num_channels)
117
118        # ==========================================================
119        # Normalization (SN3D → N3D conversion scales)
120        # ==========================================================
121
122        self._n3d_scales = self._build_normalization_scales()
123
124        # ==========================================================
125        # Stream state
126        # ==========================================================
127
128        self._current_position = 0
129
130        # ==========================================================
131        # Channel management
132        # ==========================================================
133
134        self._valid_channels: Optional[List[int]] = None
135        self._empty_channels: Optional[List[int]] = None
136
137        self._has_extra_channels = False
138        self._channel_warning_printed = False
139
140        # ==========================================================
141        # Analyze channels
142        # ==========================================================
143
144        self._setup_channel_layout(trim_extra_channels)
145        self._print_load_info()
146
147    # ==============================================================
148    # AmbiX format validation
149    # ==============================================================
150
151    def _validate_ambix_format(self):
152        """Validate that the loaded file is a valid Ambisonics audio file.
153
154        Checks performed:
155        1. File container is WAV
156        2. Channel count >= (n+1)^2 for some valid order n
157
158        The format (ambix ACN/SN3D vs FuMa WXY/Furse-Malham) is set by the
159        user via the ``format`` parameter — it cannot be auto-detected.
160        """
161
162        # Check 1: Must be a WAV file
163        if self.file.format != 'WAV':
164            raise ValueError(
165                f"Expected WAV container for Ambisonics, got '{self.file.format}'. "
166                f"Ambisonics files (ambix / FuMa) use WAV containers."
167            )
168
169        # Check 2: Channel count must be >= (n+1)^2 for some valid order n.
170        # Extra trailing channels (e.g., spot mics) are trimmed later by
171        # _setup_channel_layout — this check only ensures the file has enough
172        # channels to cover at least one valid Ambisonics order.
173        num_channels = self.num_channels
174        order_candidate = int(np.sqrt(num_channels)) - 1
175        if order_candidate < 0:
176            order_candidate = 0
177
178        if (order_candidate + 1) ** 2 > num_channels:
179            raise ValueError(
180                f"File has {num_channels} channels, which is fewer than the "
181                f"minimum 1 channel required for Ambisonics (order 0). "
182                f"This file is not a valid Ambisonics format file."
183            )
184
185        # Warm the user when channel count is not an exact (n+1)^2 match.
186        # E.g., a regular 2ch stereo WAV would reach here as "order 0 + 1 extra".
187        expected = (order_candidate + 1) ** 2
188        if num_channels != expected:
189            logger.warning(
190                "Channel count %d is not an exact (n+1)^2 value (nearest: %d). "
191                "Extra channels will be trimmed if trim_extra_channels=True. "
192                "If this is a regular multi-channel WAV (not Ambisonics), decoding "
193                "results will be incorrect.",
194                num_channels, expected,
195            )
196
197        logger.info(
198            "Ambisonics format validated: %s, %d channels, nearest order %d",
199            self.format, num_channels, order_candidate,
200        )
201
202    def set_order(self, order: int):
203        """
204        Change the Ambisonics playback order.
205
206        If the requested *order* exceeds what the current file supports
207        (requires ``(order+1)^2`` channels), it is silently clamped to the
208        highest valid order.  The channel layout is re-evaluated and extra
209        trailing channels are trimmed.
210
211        Parameters
212        ----------
213        order : int
214            Desired Ambisonics order (non-negative).
215        """
216        if order < 0:
217            raise ValueError("Order must be non-negative.")
218        
219        # make order lower if requested order is too high
220        if self.num_channels < order_to_channel_n(order):
221            # set to highest possible order instead
222            order = ambix_channels_to_order(self.num_channels)
223            print(f"Requested order too big for this file. Using highest possible order of {order} instead.")
224
225        self.order = order
226        self._validate_ambix_format()
227        self._setup_channel_layout(trim_extra_channels=True)
228
229    # ==============================================================
230    # Channel setup
231    # ==============================================================
232
233    def _setup_channel_layout(self, trim_extra_channels: bool):
234        """Determine which source channels map to the current Ambisonics order.
235
236        When the file has more channels than ``(order+1)^2`` and
237        *trim_extra_channels* is True, the extra trailing channels are
238        flagged as empty and excluded from reads.  When the file has too few
239        channels a ``ValueError`` is raised.
240
241        Parameters
242        ----------
243        trim_extra_channels : bool
244            Whether to discard trailing channels beyond the expected count.
245        """
246        expected_channels = (self.order + 1) ** 2
247
248        if self.num_channels == expected_channels:
249            self._valid_channels = list(range(self.num_channels))
250            self._empty_channels = []
251            return
252
253        logger.info("Channel mismatch: %d vs expected %d", self.num_channels, expected_channels)
254
255        if self.num_channels > expected_channels:
256            if trim_extra_channels:
257                self._valid_channels = list(range(expected_channels))
258                self._empty_channels = list(range(expected_channels, self.num_channels))
259                self._has_extra_channels = True
260                logger.info("Keeping first %d channels, discarding %d trailing channels",
261                            expected_channels, len(self._empty_channels))
262            else:
263                self._valid_channels = list(range(self.num_channels))
264                self._empty_channels = []
265                logger.warning("Keeping all channels, decoding may fail")
266        else:
267            max_order = int(np.sqrt(self.num_channels)) - 1
268            raise ValueError(
269                f"File has only {self.num_channels} channels, but Ambisonics order "
270                f"{self.order} requires {expected_channels} channels. "
271                f"The maximum order supported by this file is {max_order}. "
272                f"Please reduce the playback order or use a file with more channels.")
273
274    # ==============================================================
275    # Frame reading
276    # ==============================================================
277
278    def get_frames(
279        self,
280        start_sample: int,
281        num_samples: Optional[int] = None
282    ) -> np.ndarray:
283        """Read a block of audio frames from the underlying WAV file.
284
285        Only channels flagged as valid (see ``_setup_channel_layout``) are
286        returned.  When the normalisation is ``"N3D"``, per-ACN SN3D→N3D
287        scaling is applied in-place.
288
289        Parameters
290        ----------
291        start_sample : int
292            Zero-based sample index to seek to before reading.
293        num_samples : int or None
294            Number of samples to read.  When ``None``, defaults to the
295            current chunk size.
296
297        Returns
298        -------
299        data : ndarray of shape ``(num_samples, num_valid_channels)``, float32
300        """
301        if self.file is None:
302            raise RuntimeError("Cannot read frames: file is closed.")
303
304        if num_samples is None:
305            num_samples = self.chunk_size
306
307        if start_sample < 0:
308            logger.warning(
309                "Negative start_sample %d clamped to 0", start_sample
310            )
311            start_sample = 0
312        elif start_sample > self.total_frames:
313            logger.warning(
314                "start_sample %d exceeds total_frames %d, clamped",
315                start_sample, self.total_frames,
316            )
317            start_sample = self.total_frames
318
319        self.file.seek(start_sample)
320
321        audio_data = self.file.read(
322            frames=num_samples,
323            dtype='float32',
324            always_2d=True
325        )
326
327        # shape:
328        # (samples, channels)
329
330        if self._valid_channels is not None:
331
332            audio_data = audio_data[
333                :,
334                self._valid_channels
335            ]
336
337            if (
338                self._has_extra_channels
339                and not self._channel_warning_printed
340            ):
341
342                logger.debug(
343                    "Filtering channels: %d -> %d",
344                    self.num_channels,
345                    audio_data.shape[1]
346                )
347
348                self._channel_warning_printed = True
349
350        # Apply SN3D → N3D normalization if requested
351        if self.normalization == "N3D":
352            num_acn = len(self._n3d_scales)
353            audio_data[:, :num_acn] *= self._n3d_scales[np.newaxis, :]
354
355        return audio_data
356
357    # ==============================================================
358    # Streaming read
359    # ==============================================================
360
361    def get_next_chunk(
362        self
363    ) -> Tuple[Optional[np.ndarray], bool]:
364        """Read the next streaming chunk from the current file position.
365
366        Advances the internal position pointer by the number of samples
367        actually read.  If the chunk has more channels than expected for
368        the current order, extra channels are trimmed silently.
369
370        Returns
371        -------
372        chunk : ndarray of shape ``(samples, channels)`` or None
373            The next chunk of audio data, or ``None`` when the end of the
374            file has been reached.
375        end_of_file : bool
376            ``True`` if the returned chunk is the last one in the file.
377        """
378        if self._current_position >= self.total_frames:
379            return None, True
380
381        chunk = self.get_frames(
382            self._current_position,
383            self.chunk_size
384        )
385
386        expected_channels = order_to_channel_n(self.order)
387
388        # make sure the chunk has the correct channel count for our order
389        if chunk.shape[1] > expected_channels:
390            chunk = chunk[:, :expected_channels]
391
392        actual_samples = chunk.shape[0]
393
394        self._current_position += actual_samples
395
396        end_of_file = (
397            self._current_position >= self.total_frames
398        )
399
400        return chunk, end_of_file
401
402    # ==============================================================
403    # pyfar compatibility
404    # ==============================================================
405
406    def get_signal_chunk(
407        self,
408        start_sample: int,
409        num_samples: Optional[int] = None
410    ) -> pf.Signal:
411        """Read a block of audio and return it as a ``pyfar.Signal``.
412
413        Parameters
414        ----------
415        start_sample : int
416            Zero-based sample index to seek to before reading.
417        num_samples : int or None
418            Number of samples to read.  When ``None``, defaults to the
419            current chunk size.
420
421        Returns
422        -------
423        signal : pyfar.Signal
424            Signal in time domain with shape ``(channels, samples)``.
425        """
426
427        chunk = self.get_frames(
428            start_sample,
429            num_samples
430        )
431
432        # get_frames() returns (samples, channels)
433        # pyfar.Signal expects (channels, samples) — last dim is time
434        return pf.Signal(
435            chunk.T,
436            self.samplerate,
437            domain='time',
438            fft_norm='none'
439        )
440
441    # ==============================================================
442    # Seeking
443    # ==============================================================
444
445    def seek_to_position(self, position_samples: int):
446        """Move the streaming read pointer to an absolute sample index.
447
448        The value is clamped to ``[0, total_frames]``.
449
450        Parameters
451        ----------
452        position_samples : int
453            Target position in samples.
454        """
455
456        if position_samples < 0:
457            logger.warning("Negative position %d clamped to 0", position_samples)
458            position_samples = 0
459        elif position_samples > self.total_frames:
460            logger.warning(
461                "Position %d exceeds total_frames %d, clamped",
462                position_samples, self.total_frames,
463            )
464            position_samples = self.total_frames
465
466        self._current_position = position_samples
467
468    def seek_to_time(self, time_seconds: float):
469        """Move the streaming read pointer to a time in seconds.
470
471        Wraps ``seek_to_position`` after converting seconds to samples.
472
473        Parameters
474        ----------
475        time_seconds : float
476            Target time in seconds.
477        """
478
479        position = int(
480            time_seconds * self.samplerate
481        )
482
483        self.seek_to_position(position)
484
485    def reset_position(self):
486        """Reset the streaming read pointer to the beginning of the file."""
487        self._current_position = 0
488
489    def get_current_position(self) -> int:
490        """Return the current stream position in samples."""
491        return self._current_position
492
493    def get_current_time(self) -> float:
494        """Return the current stream position in seconds."""
495        return self._current_position / self.samplerate
496
497    # ==============================================================
498    # Info
499    # ==============================================================
500
501    def get_duration(self) -> float:
502        """Return the total audio duration in seconds."""
503        return self.duration
504
505    def get_samplerate(self) -> int:
506        """Return the sample rate in Hz."""
507        return self.samplerate
508
509    def get_order(self) -> int:
510        """Return the current Ambisonics order."""

512
513    def get_format(self) -> str:
514        """Return the Ambisonics format: 'ambix' (ACN/SN3D) or 'fuma' (WXY/Furse-Malham)."""
515        return self.format
516
517    def get_num_channels(self) -> int:
518        """Return the number of valid (non-empty) audio channels.
519
520        When extra channels have been trimmed this is ``(order+1)^2``;
521        otherwise it equals ``get_total_channels``.
522        """
523
524        if self._valid_channels is not None:
525            return len(self._valid_channels)
526
527        return self.num_channels
528
529    def get_total_channels(self) -> int:
530        """Return the total number of channels in the source file."""
531        return self.num_channels
532
533    def get_chunk_size(self) -> int:
534        """Return the current streaming chunk size in samples."""
535        return self.chunk_size
536
537    def get_normalization(self) -> str:
538        """Return the normalization scheme: 'SN3D' or 'N3D'."""
539        return self.normalization
540
541    def _build_normalization_scales(self) -> np.ndarray:
542        """Build scale factors for SN3D → N3D conversion.
543
544        For ACN channel c, order n = floor(sqrt(c)), scale = sqrt(2n + 1).
545        Returns an array of 1.0 if normalization is SN3D (no conversion needed).
546        """
547        num_acn = (self.order + 1) ** 2
548        scales = np.ones(num_acn, dtype=np.float32)
549        if self.normalization == "N3D":
550            for c in range(num_acn):
551                n = int(np.sqrt(c))
552                scales[c] = np.sqrt(2 * n + 1)
553        return scales
554
555    @staticmethod
556    def _normalize_chunk_size(chunk_size: int) -> int:
557        """Clamp *chunk_size* to [32, 8192] and round up to the nearest power of two."""
558        # Clamp to valid range
559        chunk_size = max(32, min(8192, chunk_size))
560
561        # Round up to nearest power of two: 1 << (n - 1).bit_length()
562        if chunk_size > 1:
563            chunk_size = next_power_of_two(chunk_size)
564
565        return chunk_size
566
567    def set_chunk_size(self, chunk_size: int):
568        """Update the streaming chunk size.
569
570        The value is normalised via ``_normalize_chunk_size``, so it will
571        be clamped and rounded to a power of two.
572
573        Parameters
574        ----------
575        chunk_size : int
576            Desired chunk size in samples.
577        """
578        self.chunk_size = self._normalize_chunk_size(chunk_size)
579
580        logger.info(
581            "Chunk size changed to %d",
582            self.chunk_size
583        )
584
585    # ==============================================================
586    # Validation
587    # ==============================================================
588
589    def is_valid(self) -> bool:
590        """Return True if the file has exactly ``(order+1)^2`` valid channels."""
591
592        effective = (
593            len(self._valid_channels)
594            if self._valid_channels is not None
595            else self.num_channels
596        )
597
598        expected = (self.order + 1) ** 2
599
600        return effective == expected
601
602    # ==============================================================
603    # Debug
604    # ==============================================================
605
606    def get_channel_info(self) -> dict:
607        """Return a dictionary summarising the channel layout.
608
609        Keys: total_channels, valid_channels, empty_channels,
610        effective_channels, expected_channels, has_extra_channels.
611        """
612        return {
613            'total_channels': self.num_channels,
614            'valid_channels': self._valid_channels,
615            'empty_channels': self._empty_channels,
616            'effective_channels': self.get_num_channels(),
617            'expected_channels': (self.order + 1) ** 2,
618            'has_extra_channels': self._has_extra_channels,
619        }
620
621    # ==============================================================
622    # Print info
623    # ==============================================================
624
625    def _print_load_info(self):
626        """Log a one-line summary of the loaded file (format, order, channels, duration, SR, chunk size)."""
627        effective_channels = self.get_num_channels()
628        logger.info(
629            "Loaded: %s | Format: %s | Norm: %s | Order: %d | Channels: %d -> %d | "
630            "Duration: %.2fs | SR: %d | Frames: %d | Chunk: %d",
631            self.filepath, self.format, self.normalization, self.order, self.num_channels,
632            effective_channels, self.duration, self.samplerate,
633            self.total_frames, self.chunk_size
634        )
635
636    # ==============================================================
637    # Cleanup
638    # ==============================================================
639
640    def close(self):
641        """Close the underlying soundfile handle and release resources."""
642        if self.file:
643            self.file.close()
644            self.file = None
645
646    def __enter__(self):
647        """Context-manager entry — returns self."""
648        return self
649
650    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
651        """Context-manager exit — calls ``close()``."""
652        self.close()
653
654    def __repr__(self):
655        """Return a compact string representation for debugging."""
656        return (
657            f"AmbisonicsFile(format={self.format}, norm={self.normalization}, order={self.order}, "
658            f"channels={self.get_num_channels()}, "
659            f"duration={self.duration:.2f}s, "
660            f"sr={self.samplerate})"
661        )
662
663    def __len__(self):
664        """Return the total number of frames in the file."""
665        return self.total_frames

 74            raise ValueError(
 75                f"Unsupported format '{format}'. "
 76                f"Supported: {', '.join(self._SUPPORTED_FORMATS)}."

 84            )

 95
 96        self.samplerate = self.file.samplerate
 97        self.num_channels = self.file.channels
 98        self.total_frames = len(self.file)
 99
100        self.duration = self.total_frames / self.samplerate

105
106        self._validate_ambix_format()

140        # ==========================================================

def set_order(self, order: int): 
202    def set_order(self, order: int):
203        """
204        Change the Ambisonics playback order.
205
206        If the requested *order* exceeds what the current file supports
207        (requires ``(order+1)^2`` channels), it is silently clamped to the
208        highest valid order.  The channel layout is re-evaluated and extra
209        trailing channels are trimmed.
210
211        Parameters
212        ----------
213        order : int
214            Desired Ambisonics order (non-negative).
215        """
216        if order < 0:
217            raise ValueError("Order must be non-negative.")
218        
219        # make order lower if requested order is too high
220        if self.num_channels < order_to_channel_n(order):
221            # set to highest possible order instead
222            order = ambix_channels_to_order(self.num_channels)
223            print(f"Requested order too big for this file. Using highest possible order of {order} instead.")
224
225        self.order = order
226        self._validate_ambix_format()
227        self._setup_channel_layout(trim_extra_channels=True)

def get_frames(self, start_sample: int, num_samples: int | None = None) -> numpy.ndarray: 
278    def get_frames(
279        self,
280        start_sample: int,
281        num_samples: Optional[int] = None
282    ) -> np.ndarray:
283        """Read a block of audio frames from the underlying WAV file.
284
285        Only channels flagged as valid (see ``_setup_channel_layout``) are
286        returned.  When the normalisation is ``"N3D"``, per-ACN SN3D→N3D
287        scaling is applied in-place.
288
289        Parameters
290        ----------
291        start_sample : int
292            Zero-based sample index to seek to before reading.
293        num_samples : int or None
294            Number of samples to read.  When ``None``, defaults to the
295            current chunk size.
296
297        Returns
298        -------
299        data : ndarray of shape ``(num_samples, num_valid_channels)``, float32
300        """
301        if self.file is None:
302            raise RuntimeError("Cannot read frames: file is closed.")
303
304        if num_samples is None:
305            num_samples = self.chunk_size
306
307        if start_sample < 0:
308            logger.warning(
309                "Negative start_sample %d clamped to 0", start_sample
310            )
311            start_sample = 0
312        elif start_sample > self.total_frames:
313            logger.warning(
314                "start_sample %d exceeds total_frames %d, clamped",
315                start_sample, self.total_frames,
316            )
317            start_sample = self.total_frames
318
319        self.file.seek(start_sample)
320
321        audio_data = self.file.read(
322            frames=num_samples,
323            dtype='float32',
324            always_2d=True
325        )
326
327        # shape:
328        # (samples, channels)
329
330        if self._valid_channels is not None:
331
332            audio_data = audio_data[
333                :,
334                self._valid_channels
335            ]
336
337            if (
338                self._has_extra_channels
339                and not self._channel_warning_printed
340            ):
341
342                logger.debug(
343                    "Filtering channels: %d -> %d",
344                    self.num_channels,
345                    audio_data.shape[1]
346                )
347
348                self._channel_warning_printed = True
349
350        # Apply SN3D → N3D normalization if requested
351        if self.normalization == "N3D":
352            num_acn = len(self._n3d_scales)
353            audio_data[:, :num_acn] *= self._n3d_scales[np.newaxis, :]
354
355        return audio_data

Read a block of audio frames from the underlying WAV file.

Only channels flagged as valid (see _setup_channel_layout) are returned. When the normalisation is "N3D", per-ACN SN3D→N3D scaling is applied in-place.

Parameters
  • start_sample (int): Zero-based sample index to seek to before reading.

def get_next_chunk(self) -> Tuple[numpy.ndarray | None, bool]: 
361    def get_next_chunk(
362        self
363    ) -> Tuple[Optional[np.ndarray], bool]:
364        """Read the next streaming chunk from the current file position.
365
366        Advances the internal position pointer by the number of samples
367        actually read.  If the chunk has more channels than expected for
368        the current order, extra channels are trimmed silently.
369
370        Returns
371        -------
372        chunk : ndarray of shape ``(samples, channels)`` or None
373            The next chunk of audio data, or ``None`` when the end of the
374            file has been reached.
375        end_of_file : bool
376            ``True`` if the returned chunk is the last one in the file.
377        """
378        if self._current_position >= self.total_frames:
379            return None, True
380
381        chunk = self.get_frames(
382            self._current_position,
383            self.chunk_size
384        )
385
386        expected_channels = order_to_channel_n(self.order)
387
388        # make sure the chunk has the correct channel count for our order
389        if chunk.shape[1] > expected_channels:
390            chunk = chunk[:, :expected_channels]
391
392        actual_samples = chunk.shape[0]
393
394        self._current_position += actual_samples
395
396        end_of_file = (
397            self._current_position >= self.total_frames
398        )
399
400        return chunk, end_of_file

407        self,
408        start_sample: int,

410    ) -> pf.Signal:
411        """Read a block of audio and return it as a ``pyfar.Signal``.
412
413        Parameters
414        ----------
415        start_sample : int
416            Zero-based sample index to seek to before reading.
417        num_samples : int or None
418            Number of samples to read.  When ``None``, defaults to the
419            current chunk size.
420
421        Returns
422        -------

424            Signal in time domain with shape ``(channels, samples)``.
425        """
426
427        chunk = self.get_frames(
428            start_sample,

430        )
431
432        # get_frames() returns (samples, channels)
433        # pyfar.Signal expects (channels, samples) — last dim is time
434        return pf.Signal(
435            chunk.T,
436            self.samplerate,
437            domain='time',
438            fft_norm='none'
439        )

class AudioPlayer: 
 13class AudioPlayer:
 14    """
 15    Streaming audio player for GUI control.
 16
 17    Supports:
 18    - load WAV
 19    - load NumPy audio array
 20    - load pyfar.Signal
 21    - play
 22    - pause / resume
 23    - stop
 24    - real-time volume control
 25    - start offset
 26    - seek with progress bar
 27    - loop playback
 28    """
 29
 30    def __init__(self, ambi_file: AmbisonicsFile, sh: SphericalHarmonics, gain=1.0):
 31        self.position = 0
 32        self.is_loaded = False
 33        self.source_name = None
 34        
 35        # Check channel count by comparing the channel shape
 36        # we know the channel shape for sh_hrir is (2, channels)
 37        _, sh_hrir_ch, _ = sh.hrir_nm.shape
 38        if ambi_file.get_num_channels() != sh_hrir_ch:
 39            raise ValueError("Channel counts must match (e.g. 16 for 3rd order).")
 40        
 41        if gain > 1. or gain < 0:
 42            raise AttributeError("The gain must be in range [0., 1.].")
 43        
 44        # spherical processing of ambisonics file instances
 45        self.ambi_file = ambi_file
 46        self.sh = sh
 47        # some important internal variables
 48        self.gain = gain
 49        self.fs = ambi_file.get_samplerate()
 50        # binarual is always stereo
 51        self.n_channels = 2
 52
 53        self.audio_queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=10)
 54
 55        # some control flags for handling playing, stopping and pausing
 56        self.play_event = threading.Event()
 57        self.stop_event = threading.Event()
 58        self.pause_event = threading.Event()
 59        self.seek_event = threading.Event()
 60        self.seek_target = 0.0
 61        self.loop = False
 62
 63        # keeping track of blocks
 64        self.current_block = None
 65        self.current_block_pos = 0
 66
 67        # Thread and stream objects
 68        self.processing_thread = None
 69        self.stream = None
 70        # construction received a valid, validated source: ready to play
 71        self.is_loaded = True
 72
 73    def _put_stop_aware(self, item) -> bool:
 74        """
 75        Put an item into the audio queue, waiting while playback is alive.
 76
 77        Returns False (without putting) once stop_event is set, so the
 78        processing thread never blocks past a stop and never drops blocks.
 79        """
 80        while not self.stop_event.is_set():
 81            try:
 82                self.audio_queue.put(item, timeout=0.1)
 83                return True
 84            except queue.Full:
 85                continue
 86        return False
 87    
 88    def update_process_variables(self):
 89        """
 90        Wraps Spherical Harmonics process variables update
 91        """
 92        self.sh.update_process_variables(self.ambi_file.get_chunk_size())
 93        
 94    def _process_loop(self):
 95        """Processing thread: reads chunks, processes, and puts into queue."""
 96        
 97        print("Start processing thread.")
 98
 99        # ensures we only wait a fraction of the time we generally need
100        #put_timeout = (self.block_size / self.fs) * 0.1
101
102        # while we are not stopping
103        while not self.stop_event.is_set():
104
105            # seek handling: update current time and internal state
106            if self.seek_event.is_set():
107                # clear the seek event
108                self.seek_event.clear()
109                self.current_block = None
110                self.current_block_pos = 0
111                self._clear_audio_queue()
112                self.ambi_file.seek_to_time(self.seek_target)
113                self.sh.update_process_variables(self.ambi_file.get_chunk_size())
114                #continue to enxt loop iteration
115                continue
116
117            # Pause handling: block if paused but not stopped
118            if self.pause_event.is_set():
119                # Wait for play_event (resume or stop) with a bounded timeout
120                # so a stop racing past this check cannot strand the thread.
121                while not self.play_event.wait(timeout=0.1):
122                    if self.stop_event.is_set():
123                        break
124            
125                # If stop was triggered, exit the outer loop
126                if self.stop_event.is_set():
127                    break
128
129            # Read next chunk
130            chunk, end_of_file = self.ambi_file.get_next_chunk()
131            if chunk is None:
132                break
133            
134            # processes one chunk and return a stereo block, 
135            # updating the overlap buffer internally.
136            processed_block = self.sh.process_ola(chunk)
137
138            # # Put into queue (waits instead of dropping; aborts on stop)
139            # if not self._put_stop_aware(processed_block):
140            #     break
141
142            # Put into queue
143            try:
144                self.audio_queue.put(processed_block, timeout=0.1)
145            except queue.Full:
146                # probably the playback was stopped or paused. in this case we can safely drop the block without notifying
147                if not self.pause_event.is_set() and not self.stop_event.is_set():
148                    # if not we print a warning
149                    print("Warning!!! Queue is full! Dropping this block")
150
151            # at end of file flush any remaining output from SH-overlap-buffer
152            if end_of_file:
153                if not self._put_stop_aware(self.sh.flush()):
154                    break
155
156                #check for looping
157                if self.loop:
158                    # resets processor and will read chunk 0 next
159                    self.sh.update_process_variables(self.ambi_file.get_chunk_size())
160                    self.ambi_file.reset_position()
161                else:
162                    # queue None-item as flag that playback has ended
163                    if not self._put_stop_aware(None):
164                        break
165                    # clear the play event
166                    self.play_event.clear()
167
168    def load_audio(self, audio, sample_rate, source_name="Audio array"):
169        """
170        Load audio directly from a NumPy array.
171
172        Internal format:
173        audio.shape == (samples, 2)
174        """
175
176        audio = np.asarray(audio, dtype="float32")
177
178        # Mono to stereo
179        if audio.ndim == 1:
180            audio = np.column_stack((audio, audio))
181
182        # Convert (channels, samples) to (samples, channels)
183        # This is useful for pyfar.Signal, which may use (2, samples)
184        if audio.ndim == 2 and audio.shape[0] == 2 and audio.shape[1] > 2:
185            audio = audio.T
186
187        # Player only accepts binaural stereo signal
188        if audio.ndim != 2 or audio.shape[1] != 2:
189            raise ValueError(
190                f"Player expects stereo audio with shape (samples, 2), "
191                f"but got {audio.shape}"
192            )
193
194        # Avoid clipping
195        max_value = np.max(np.abs(audio))
196        if max_value > 1.0:
197            audio = audio / max_value
198            print("Audio was normalized to avoid clipping.")
199
200        # Stop previous playback before loading new audio
201        self.stop()
202
203        self.audio = audio
204        self.fs = int(sample_rate)
205        self.position = 0
206        self.is_loaded = True
207        self.source_name = source_name
208
209        print("\nAudio loaded successfully.")
210        self.print_info()
211
212    def load_wav(self, file_path: str):
213        """
214        Load a WAV file from disk.
215        """
216
217        audio, sample_rate = sf.read(file_path, dtype="float32")
218        self.load_audio(audio, sample_rate, source_name=file_path)
219
220    def load_pyfar_signal(self, signal):
221        """
222        Load audio from a pyfar.Signal object.
223
224        Expected:
225        - signal.time contains audio data
226        - signal.sampling_rate contains the sampling rate
227        """
228
229        audio = signal.time
230        sample_rate = signal.sampling_rate
231        self.load_audio(audio, sample_rate, source_name="pyfar.Signal")
232
233    def _audio_callback_robust(self, outdata, frames, time, status):
234        """sounddevice callback – outputs from queue or silence if paused."""
235
236        # debug if something went wrong last callback
237        if status:
238            print(f"Audio callback status: {status}")
239
240        # check pasue status
241        if self.pause_event.is_set():
242            # fill with silence if paused
243            outdata.fill(0)
244            return
245        
246        # prepare output buffer for this callback
247        out = np.zeros((frames, self.n_channels), dtype=np.float32)
248        need = frames
249        write_pos = 0
250
251        while need > 0:
252            # if no curent block is availabel or it hasn't been fully consumed yet, process a new block
253            if self.current_block is None or self.current_block_pos >= len(self.current_block):
254                try:
255                    data = self.audio_queue.get_nowait()
256                except queue.Empty:
257                    print("Audio queue underrun: outputting silence")
258                    # Underflow: not enough processed audio ready: output 0's
259                    outdata[:] = out * self.gain
260                    return
261                
262                # we set data = None in our _process_loop() if we reached the end of file to signal playback has ended
263                if data is None:
264                    # End of file
265                    outdata.fill(0)
266                    # tell sounddevice to cleanup and stop the callback
267                    raise sd.CallbackStop
268                
269                # ensure shape (n_samples, n_channels) and correct dtype
270                self.current_block = np.asarray(data, dtype=np.float32)
271                self.current_block_pos = 0
272
273            # write the current block to output
274            # get sample counts for writing
275            available = len(self.current_block) - self.current_block_pos
276            take = min(available, need)
277            
278            # copy current block to output buffer
279            out[write_pos:write_pos + take] = self.current_block[self.current_block_pos:self.current_block_pos + take]
280            self.current_block_pos += take
281            write_pos += take
282            need -= take
283
284        # write output to outdata
285        outdata[:] = out * self.gain
286
287    def play(self):
288        """
289        Start or resume playback.
290        """
291
292        if not self.is_loaded:
293            print("No audio loaded.")
294            return
295
296        # If currently paused, resume
297        if self.pause_event.is_set():
298            self.resume()
299            return
300
301        # If already playing, do nothing
302        if self.stream is not None and self.play_event.is_set():
303            print("Already playing.")
304            return
305
306        # If stream exists but is not playing, close it first
307        if self.stream is not None:
308            self.stop()
309
310        # reset stop and pause flags
311        self.stop_event.clear()
312        self.pause_event.clear()
313
314        # reset all processing variables before starting the processing thread. 
315        # also ensures block size is calculated before we initialize the stream
316        self.sh.update_process_variables(self.ambi_file.get_chunk_size())
317
318        # Start processing thread
319        self.processing_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._process_loop)
320        self.processing_thread.start()
321
322        self.stream = sd.OutputStream(
323            samplerate=self.fs,
324            channels=self.n_channels,
325            dtype="float32",
326            callback=self._audio_callback_robust,
327            # let sounddevice choose blocksize
328            # blocksize=self.N,
329            finished_callback=self._on_stream_finished
330        )
331
332        # set palying flag to true
333        self.play_event.set()
334
335        print(f"Playing from {self.ambi_file.get_current_time():.2f} seconds...")
336        self.stream.start()
337
338    def _on_stream_finished(self):
339        """Called when stream stops (e.g., at end of file)."""
340        print("Stream finished.")
341        # set the stop flag
342        self.stop_event.set()
343
344    def pause(self):
345        """
346        Pause playback and keep current position.
347        """
348
349        if not self.play_event.is_set():
350            return
351
352        self.pause_event.set()
353        self.play_event.clear()
354        
355        print(f"Paused at {self.ambi_file.get_current_time():.2f} seconds.")
356
357    def resume(self):
358        """
359        Resume playback from current position.
360        """
361
362        if not self.is_loaded:
363            return
364
365        self.pause_event.clear()
366
367        if self.stream is None:
368            self.play()
369        else:
370            self.play_event.set()
371            print(f"Resumed at {self.ambi_file.get_current_time():.2f} seconds.")
372
373    def stop(self, reset_position=True):
374        """
375        Stop playback. Clears the stream and the processing thread. Call this before exiting the program.
376
377        Parameters
378        ----------
379        reset_position : bool
380            If True, reset playback position to the beginning.
381        """
382
383        # set the stop flag
384        self.stop_event.set()
385        # clear the pause flag, just in case it was blocking our processing thread
386        self.pause_event.clear()
387        # set the play flag to true, to wake the waiting processing thread
388        self.play_event.set()
389
390        # clean up the stream
391        if self.stream is not None:
392            self.stream.stop()
393            self.stream.close()
394            self.stream = None
395
396        # terminate the processing_thread
397        if self.processing_thread is not None:
398            self.processing_thread.join(timeout=1.0)
399
400            # debug message if processing_thread didn't terminate properly
401            if self.processing_thread.is_alive():
402                print("Warning: Processing thread did not terminate cleanly.")
403
404        # Clear queue
405        while not self.audio_queue.empty():
406            try:
407                self.audio_queue.get_nowait()
408            except queue.Empty:
409                break
410
411        if reset_position:
412            self.ambi_file.reset_position()
413
414        # clear the play event at the end
415        self.play_event.clear()
416        print("Playback stopped.")
417
418    def close(self):
419        """
420        Closes the player completely, preparing it for termination. The player cannot be used after calling this.
421        """
422        self.stop()
423        self.sh.close()
424
425    def set_volume(self, volume: float):
426        """
427        Set playback volume between 0.0 and 1.0.
428        """
429
430        self.gain = max(0.0, min(float(volume), 1.0))
431        print(f"Volume set to {self.gain:.2f}")
432
433    def set_start_offset(self, seconds: float):
434        """
435        Set the playback start position in seconds.
436        """
437
438        if not self.is_loaded:
439            print("No audio loaded.")
440            return
441
442        duration = self.get_duration()
443
444        if seconds >= duration:
445            print(f"Offset is too large. Audio duration is only {duration:.2f} seconds.")
446            return
447        
448        # in case we are not already streaming/processing data just update internal state
449        if self.stream is None or self.processing_thread is None:
450            self.sh.update_process_variables(self.ambi_file.get_chunk_size())
451            self.ambi_file.seek_to_time(seconds)
452            self._clear_audio_queue()
453            self.position = int(seconds * self.fs)
454            print(f"Seeked to {seconds:.2f} seconds.")
455            return
456
457        self._request_seek(seconds)
458        self.position = int(seconds * self.fs)
459        print(f"Seek requested to {seconds:.2f} seconds.")
460
461    def seek_to(self, seconds: float):
462        """
463        Jump to a specific playback position in seconds.
464        This is mainly used by the GUI progress bar.
465        """
466
467        if not self.is_loaded:
468            print("No audio loaded.")
469            return
470        
471        duration = self.get_duration()
472
473        if seconds >= duration:
474            print(f"Offset is too large. Audio duration is only {duration:.2f} seconds.")
475            return
476
477        # in case we are not already streaming/processing data just update internal state
478        if self.stream is None or self.processing_thread is None:
479            self.sh.update_process_variables(self.ambi_file.get_chunk_size())
480            self.ambi_file.seek_to_time(seconds)
481            self._clear_audio_queue()
482            self.position = int(seconds * self.fs)
483            print(f"Seeked to {seconds:.2f} seconds.")
484            return
485
486        self._request_seek(seconds)
487        self.position = int(seconds * self.fs)
488        print(f"Seek requested to {seconds:.2f} seconds.")
489
490    def _clear_audio_queue(self):
491        """
492        Drains and discards all queued items in the audio_queue
493        """
494        while not self.audio_queue.empty():
495            try:
496                # drain the next item in the queue
497                self.audio_queue.get_nowait()
498            except queue.Empty:
499                # exit when queue is empty
500                break
501
502    def _request_seek(self, seconds: float):
503        self.seek_target = max(0.0, min(seconds, self.get_duration()))
504        self.current_block = None
505        self.current_block_pos = 0
506        self._clear_audio_queue()
507        self.seek_event.set()
508
509    def set_loop(self, enabled: bool):
510        """
511        Enable or disable loop playback.
512        """
513
514        self.loop = bool(enabled)
515        print(f"Loop set to {self.loop}")
516
517    def get_duration(self):
518        """
519        Return total duration in seconds.
520        """
521
522        if not self.is_loaded:
523            return 0.0
524
525        return self.ambi_file.get_duration()
526
527    def get_current_time(self):
528        """
529        Return current playback time in seconds.
530        """
531
532        if not self.is_loaded:
533            return 0.0
534        
535        # in case we are currently in a seek event: update time correctly
536        if self.seek_event.is_set():
537            return self.seek_target
538
539        return self.ambi_file.get_current_time()
540
541    def get_info_text(self):
542        """
543        Return audio information as formatted text.
544        """
545
546        if not self.is_loaded:
547            return "No audio loaded."
548
549        return (
550            f"Source: {self.source_name}\n"
551            f"Sample rate: {self.fs} Hz\n"
552            f"Channels: {self.ambi_file.get_num_channels()}\n"
553            f"Duration: {self.get_duration():.2f} seconds\n"
554            f"Current time: {self.get_current_time():.2f} seconds\n"
555            f"Current volume: {self.gain:.2f}\n"
556            f"Loop: {self.loop}"
557        )
558
559    def print_info(self):
560        """
561        Print audio information.
562        """
563
564        print(self.get_info_text())
565
566    def set_loaded(self, loaded: bool):
567        self.is_loaded = loaded

Streaming audio player for GUI control.

Supports:

  • load WAV
  • load NumPy audio array
  • load pyfar.Signal
  • play
  • pause / resume
  • stop
  • real-time volume control
  • start offset
  • seek with progress bar
  • loop playback
AudioPlayer( ambi_file: AmbisonicsFile, sh: SphericalHarmonics, gain=1.0) 
30    def __init__(self, ambi_file: AmbisonicsFile, sh: SphericalHarmonics, gain=1.0):
31        self.position = 0
32        self.is_loaded = False
33        self.source_name = None
34        
35        # Check channel count by comparing the channel shape
36        # we know the channel shape for sh_hrir is (2, channels)
37        _, sh_hrir_ch, _ = sh.hrir_nm.shape
38        if ambi_file.get_num_channels() != sh_hrir_ch:
39            raise ValueError("Channel counts must match (e.g. 16 for 3rd order).")
40        
41        if gain > 1. or gain < 0:
42            raise AttributeError("The gain must be in range [0., 1.].")
43        
44        # spherical processing of ambisonics file instances
45        self.ambi_file = ambi_file
46        self.sh = sh
47        # some important internal variables
48        self.gain = gain
49        self.fs = ambi_file.get_samplerate()
50        # binarual is always stereo
51        self.n_channels = 2
52
53        self.audio_queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=10)
54
55        # some control flags for handling playing, stopping and pausing
56        self.play_event = threading.Event()
57        self.stop_event = threading.Event()
58        self.pause_event = threading.Event()
59        self.seek_event = threading.Event()
60        self.seek_target = 0.0
61        self.loop = False
62
63        # keeping track of blocks
64        self.current_block = None
65        self.current_block_pos = 0
66
67        # Thread and stream objects
68        self.processing_thread = None
69        self.stream = None
70        # construction received a valid, validated source: ready to play
71        self.is_loaded = True

class HRTF: 
 11class HRTF:
 12    """
 13    Load and manage Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF) data with preprocessing.
 14
 15    This class handles complete HRTF dataset management: loads HRIR/HRTF data 
 16    from SOFA files (with fallback to web download), supports resampling, 
 17    applies headphone compensation filters, and provides diffuse-field 
 18    equalization. Maintains both original unmodified HRIRs and a working 
 19    copy that can be modified by filters.
 20
 21    Parameters
 22    ----------
 23    path : str, pathlib.Path, or None, optional
 24        Path to a SOFA file containing HRTF/HRIR data. If None, uses the
 25        default FABIAN HRTF dataset (specified by DEFAULT_HRTF_FILE).
 26        If loading fails locally, attempts web download. Default is None.
 27
 28    Attributes
 29    ----------
 30    path : pathlib.Path or None
 31        Resolved filesystem path to the loaded SOFA file. None if path
 32        could not be resolved.
 33    hrirs : pf.Signal
 34        Working HRIR signals (may be modified by filters).
 35        Shape: (n_directions, n_channels).
 36    hrirs_linear : pf.Signal
 37        Original unmodified HRIR signals (never modified).
 38        Use reset_hrirs() to restore hrirs to this state.
 39    sources : np.ndarray
 40        Spatial source coordinates (direction/elevation) of HRIR measurements.
 41    fs : int
 42        Current sampling rate in Hz.
 43    hp_list : list of str
 44        Available headphone filter names (FABIAN dataset only).
 45        Always includes "Diffuse Field Equalization".
 46    current_filter : str or None
 47        Name of currently applied headphone filter (None if none active).
 48    resources : pathlib.Path
 49        Path to the application's resources directory.
 50    hp_dir : pathlib.Path
 51        Path to the Headphones subdirectory containing filter definitions.
 52    app_dir : pathlib.Path
 53        Root application directory.
 54
 55    Methods
 56    -------
 57    resample(fs, truncate=True)
 58        Resample HRIRs to a new sampling rate.
 59    load_hp_filter(name, min_phase=True, n_samples=512)
 60        Load and apply a headphone compensation filter.
 61    reset_hrirs()
 62        Restore HRIRs to unmodified state.
 63    apply_dfe()
 64        Apply Diffuse Field Equalization.
 65    get_IR_length(linear=False)
 66        Get impulse-response length in samples.
 67
 68    Notes
 69    -----
 70    - FABIAN HRTF dataset is used by default
 71    - Headphone filters are only available if using FABIAN dataset
 72    - self.hrirs_linear is always preserved; modifications affect only self.hrirs
 73    - Resampling with truncate=True is recommended for real-time performance
 74    - DFE and minimum-phase conversions are available for perceptual optimization
 75
 76    Examples
 77    --------
 78    >>> hrtf = HRTF()  # Load default FABIAN
 79    >>> hrtf.resample(48000)
 80    >>> hrtf.load_hp_filter("AKG K701")
 81    >>> ir_length = hrtf.get_IR_length()
 82    """
 83
 84    def __init__(self, path=None):
 85        """
 86        Initialize an HRTF instance and load HRTF data from file or web.
 87        
 88        Attempts to load Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF) data from the
 89        provided SOFA file path. On failure, falls back to downloading the
 90        default FABIAN HRTF dataset from the internet. Also initializes the
 91        list of available headphone compensation filters.
 92
 93        Parameters
 94        ----------
 95        path : str, pathlib.Path, or None, optional
 96            Path to a SOFA file containing HRTF/HRIR data. If None, uses
 97            the default FABIAN HRTF path specified by DEFAULT_HRTF_FILE.
 98            Default is None.
 99
100        Raises
101        ------
102        Exception
103            If both local and web loading fail (propagated from load_HRTF).
104
105        Notes
106        -----
107        - self.hrirs_linear stores the unmodified original HRIRs
108        - self.hrirs can be modified by load_hp_filter() or reset via reset_hrirs()
109        - Available headphone filters are stored in self.hp_list
110        """
111        self.app_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent.parent
112        if path is None:    
113            path = DEFAULT_HRTF_FILE
114        self.path = resolve_path(path)
115
116        # load HRTF from files
117        self.hrirs, self.sources = self.load_HRTF()
118        self.hrirs_linear = self.hrirs.copy()
119
120        # keep track of the sampling rate
121        self.fs = self.hrirs.sampling_rate
122
123        # make a list of all subdirectories of our Headphone filters
124        self.resources = self.app_dir / "resources"
125        self.hp_dir = self.resources / "Headphones"
126        hp_subdir = [x for x in self.hp_dir.iterdir() if x.is_dir()] if self.hp_dir.exists() else []
127        # check if this is the FABIAN HRTF Dataset. in that case we have headphone filters for it
128        if self.path.name == Path(DEFAULT_HRTF_FILE):
129            self.hp_list = [x.name for x in hp_subdir]
130        else:
131            self.hp_list = []
132        self.hp_list.append("Diffuse Field Equalization")
133
134        # store the current HP filter name
135        self.current_filter = None
136
137    def resample(self, fs, truncate=True):
138        """
139        Resample the HRTF data to a target sampling rate.
140        
141        Resamples both self.hrirs and self.hrirs_linear to match the target
142        sampling rate. By default, truncates on upsampling to maintain the
143        original sample count for performance.
144
145        Parameters
146        ----------
147        fs : int or float
148            Target sampling rate in Hz.
149        truncate : bool, optional
150            If True and upsampling increases sample count, truncate the signal
151            back to its original length using a fade-out window. Default is True.
152
153        Notes
154        -----
155        - Uses pyfar's resample with 'freq' amplitude matching
156        - Truncation applies a right-side kaiser(8) window fade
157        - self.fs is updated to reflect the new sampling rate
158        """
159
160        if fs != self.fs:
161            self.hrirs = self._resample_save(self.hrirs, fs, truncate)
162            self.hrirs_linear = self._resample_save(self.hrirs_linear, fs, truncate)
163            self.fs = fs
164
165    def _resample_save(self, signal: pf.Signal, fs, truncate=True):
166        """
167        Resample a pyfar Signal to a target rate with optional truncation.
168        
169        Internal helper that resamples a single pyfar Signal and optionally
170        truncates it back to its original sample count to manage file size.
171
172        Parameters
173        ----------
174        signal : pf.Signal
175            Input signal to resample.
176        fs : int or float
177            Target sampling rate in Hz.
178        truncate : bool, optional
179            If True and upsampling occurs, trim the signal to its original
180            length using a kaiser-windowed fade. Default is True.
181
182        Returns
183        -------
184        pf.Signal
185            Resampled (and possibly truncated) signal.
186
187        Notes
188        -----
189        - Helper for resample() method
190        - Truncation uses a right-side fade to blend the edge smoothly
191        """
192        # current samplecount
193        n_samples = signal.n_samples
194
195        # resample hrirs
196        signal = pf.dsp.resample(signal, 
197                                sampling_rate=fs, 
198                                match_amplitude='freq'
199                                )
200        
201        # truncate the signal if desired to shorter signal after upsampling for performance
202        if truncate and n_samples < signal.n_samples:
203            extra = signal.n_samples - n_samples
204
205            # fade out the signal first
206            signal = pf.dsp.time_window(signal, (n_samples-extra, n_samples-1), shape='right')
207            # then crop (borken for some reason)
208            #signal = pf.dsp.time_crop(signal, (0, n_samples))
209
210            # use the pyfar implementation until the bug is fixed
211            indices = np.arange(signal.n_samples)
212            mask = ((indices >= 0) & (indices <= n_samples))
213            time_data = signal.time[..., mask]
214            signal = pf.Signal(time_data, signal.sampling_rate)
215
216        return signal
217
218    def get_IR_length(self, linear=False):
219        """
220        Return the impulse-response length in samples of the loaded HRIRs.
221
222        Parameters
223        ----------
224        linear : bool, optional
225            If True, return the sample count of the original unmodified HRIRs
226            (self.hrirs_linear). If False, return the count for the current
227            (possibly filtered) HRIRs. Default is False.
228        
229        Returns
230        -------
231        int
232            Number of samples in the HRIR time-domain representation.
233
234        Notes
235        -----
236        - Call this after resample() to get the updated length
237        - linear=True is useful to check original IR length before filtering
238        """
239        
240        # returns the length of the HRTF impulse response
241        if linear:
242            return self.hrirs_linear.n_samples
243        
244        return self.hrirs.n_samples
245
246    def load_HRTF(self):
247        """
248        Load HRTF data from a SOFA file or fall back to a web download.
249
250        Returns
251        -------
252        tuple
253            A tuple ``(hrirs, sources)`` where `hrirs` is a :class:`pyfar.Signal`
254            containing the HRIRs and `sources` is an ndarray with source
255            coordinates. If loading fails, both values may be `None`.
256            
257        Notes
258        ----------
259        If local loading fails, load_hrtf_from_web() is invoked as a fallback.
260        """
261        if self.path is not None:
262            # load HRIRs and source positions
263            try:
264                hrirs, sources, _ = pf.io.read_sofa(self.path)
265                print(f"Loaded HRTF from file: {self.path}")
266                return hrirs, sources
267            except Exception as e:
268                print(f"Couldn't load the HRTF from file. Exception: {e}\nAttempting to load from web instead. ")
269
270        # try to load HRTF from web
271        return self.load_hrtf_from_web()
272
273    # loads HRTFs from the internet
274    def load_hrtf_from_web(self):
275        """
276        Download and load the FABIAN HRTF SOFA file.
277
278        Returns
279        -------
280        tuple
281            A tuple ``(hrirs, sources)`` where `hrirs` is a :class:`pyfar.Signal`
282            containing the HRIRs and `sources` is an ndarray with source
283            coordinates. If loading fails, both values may be `None`.
284        """
285
286        # Leave this as it is: This is the URL from which the data will be downloaded
287        # and a hash for checking if the download worked.
288        url = 'https://github.com/pyfar/files/raw/refs/heads/main/education/VAR_TUB/FABIAN_HRIR_measured_HATO_0.sofa?download='
289        hash = '83ebbcd9a09d17679b95d201c9775438c0bb1199d565c3fc7a25448a905cdc3c'
290
291        file = pooch.retrieve(
292            url, hash, fname='FABIAN_HRIR_measured_HATO_0.sofa', path=None)
293
294        # load HRIRs and source positions
295        hrirs, sources, _ = pf.io.read_sofa(file)
296        print("Loaded HRTF from web")
297        return hrirs, sources
298    
299    # loads a specific headphone filter given by the path
300    # applies it to the hrir loaded
301    def load_hp_filter(self, name, min_phase=True, n_samples=512):
302        """
303        Load a headphone compensation filter by name and apply it to current HRIRs.
304        
305        Parameters
306        -------------
307        name : str
308            Subdirectory name under Headphones identifying the headphone.
309        min_phase : bool, optional
310            A boolean telling the function to use minimum phase conversion of the headphone filter. If true, 
311            the filter will be converted to minimum phase, resulting in a way shorter filter signal, and making
312            real time computation possible. By default minimum phase conversion is turned on.
313        n_samples : int, optional
314            An integer indicating the desired length of the resulting min HRIR
315
316        Returns
317        -------------
318        pyfar.Signal
319            Loaded headphone filter signal.
320
321        Notes
322        -------------------
323        Attempts to read a SOFA filter first and falls back to loading a WAV filter if needed.
324        The loaded filter is convolved with self.hrirs before returning.
325        """
326
327        if name in (None, "", "None"):
328            self.reset_hrirs()
329            self.current_filter = None
330            return None
331        
332        # do Diffuse Field Equalization as default
333        if name == "Diffuse Field Equalization":
334            self.current_filter = name
335            return self.apply_dfe()
336
337        path = self.hp_dir / name
338        if not path.exists():
339            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Headphone filter folder not found: {path}")
340
341        # load headphoen filter as WAV
342        hp_filter = pf.io.read_audio(path / "HpFilter.wav")
343        if isinstance(hp_filter, tuple):
344            hp_filter = hp_filter[0]
345        print(f"Loaded Headphone Filter {name} from wav")
346
347        # resample if needed
348        if hp_filter.sampling_rate != self.fs:
349            hp_filter = pf.dsp.resample(
350                hp_filter,
351                self.fs,
352                match_amplitude="freq",
353            )
354        
355        # apply minimum phase conversion
356        if min_phase:
357            desired_length = n_samples - self.get_IR_length(linear=True)
358            if desired_length <= 0:
359                raise ValueError(
360                    "n_samples must be larger than the linear HRIR length for minimum-phase headphone filtering."
361                )
362            # apply it before convolution to the hp_filter
363            hp_filter = pf.dsp.minimum_phase(hp_filter)
364
365            # apply a kaiser window to our filter, makin the filter 'n_samples' long
366            hp_filter = pf.dsp.time_window(hp_filter, 
367                                            (0, desired_length-1), 
368                                            window=('kaiser', 8), 
369                                            shape='right', 
370                                            crop='window')
371            
372        # apply headphone filter to hrirs
373        self.hrirs = pf.dsp.convolve(self.hrirs_linear, hp_filter, mode='full')
374        self.current_filter = name
375        return hp_filter
376    
377    # sets hrirs to hrirs_linear
378    def reset_hrirs(self):
379        """
380        Restore the original unmodified HRIRs.
381        
382        Resets self.hrirs to the copy stored in self.hrirs_linear, undoing
383        any headphone filter convolution or other modifications. Useful for
384        switching between filter presets.
385
386        Notes
387        -----
388        - Does not reset self.current_filter; call load_hp_filter(None) for that
389        - Original HRIRs are always preserved in self.hrirs_linear
390        """
391        self.hrirs = self.hrirs_linear.copy()
392
393    def apply_dfe(self):
394        """
395        Apply Diffuse Field Equalization (DFE) to the HRIRs.
396        
397        Computes a minimum-phase DFE filter by averaging all HRIRs, inverting
398        the average response, and convolving the result with the original
399        unmodified HRIRs. This equalizes frequency-response variations across
400        directions.
401
402        Returns
403        -------
404        pf.Signal
405            The minimum-phase DFE filter applied to self.hrirs_linear.
406
407        Notes
408        -----
409        - Uses regularized spectrum inversion with frequency range [50 Hz, 16 kHz]
410        - Sets self.hrirs to the equalized result
411        - DFE is a standard preprocessing for improved binaural quality
412        - Computation may be slow for large HRTF datasets
413        """
414        # averaging each HRTF with the average of all HRTF
415        average = pf.dsp.average(self.hrirs_linear, mode='power',caxis=0)
416        # Inversion
417        regularized = pf.dsp.RegularizedSpectrumInversion.from_frequency_range(
418            average, [50, 16e3], beta='max')
419        inverted = regularized.invert
420        # minimum phase
421        min_phase_dfe = pf.dsp.minimum_phase(inverted, truncate=False)
422
423        # convolve hrirs with the dfe filter
424        self.hrirs = pf.dsp.convolve(self.hrirs_linear, min_phase_dfe, mode='full')
425
426        return min_phase_dfe

Load and manage Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF) data with preprocessing.

This class handles complete HRTF dataset management: loads HRIR/HRTF data from SOFA files (with fallback to web download), supports resampling, applies headphone compensation filters, and provides diffuse-field equalization. Maintains both original unmodified HRIRs and a working copy that can be modified by filters.

Parameters
  • path (str, pathlib.Path, or None, optional): Path to a SOFA file containing HRTF/HRIR data. If None, uses the default FABIAN HRTF dataset (specified by DEFAULT_HRTF_FILE). If loading fails locally, attempts web download. Default is None.
Attributes
  • path (pathlib.Path or None): Resolved filesystem path to the loaded SOFA file. None if path could not be resolved.
  • hrirs (pf.Signal): Working HRIR signals (may be modified by filters). Shape: (n_directions, n_channels).
  • hrirs_linear (pf.Signal): Original unmodified HRIR signals (never modified). Use reset_hrirs() to restore hrirs to this state.
  • sources (np.ndarray): Spatial source coordinates (direction/elevation) of HRIR measurements.
  • fs (int): Current sampling rate in Hz.
  • hp_list (list of str): Available headphone filter names (FABIAN dataset only). Always includes "Diffuse Field Equalization".
  • current_filter (str or None): Name of currently applied headphone filter (None if none active).
  • resources (pathlib.Path): Path to the application's resources directory.
  • hp_dir (pathlib.Path): Path to the Headphones subdirectory containing filter definitions.
  • app_dir (pathlib.Path): Root application directory.
Methods

resample(fs, truncate=True) Resample HRIRs to a new sampling rate. load_hp_filter(name, min_phase=True, n_samples=512) Load and apply a headphone compensation filter. reset_hrirs() Restore HRIRs to unmodified state. apply_dfe() Apply Diffuse Field Equalization. get_IR_length(linear=False) Get impulse-response length in samples.

Notes
  • FABIAN HRTF dataset is used by default
  • Headphone filters are only available if using FABIAN dataset
  • self.hrirs_linear is always preserved; modifications affect only self.hrirs
  • Resampling with truncate=True is recommended for real-time performance
  • DFE and minimum-phase conversions are available for perceptual optimization
Examples
>>> hrtf = HRTF()  # Load default FABIAN
>>> hrtf.resample(48000)
>>> hrtf.load_hp_filter("AKG K701")
>>> ir_length = hrtf.get_IR_length()

def resample(self, fs, truncate=True): 
137    def resample(self, fs, truncate=True):
138        """
139        Resample the HRTF data to a target sampling rate.
140        
141        Resamples both self.hrirs and self.hrirs_linear to match the target
142        sampling rate. By default, truncates on upsampling to maintain the
143        original sample count for performance.
144
145        Parameters
146        ----------
147        fs : int or float
148            Target sampling rate in Hz.
149        truncate : bool, optional
150            If True and upsampling increases sample count, truncate the signal
151            back to its original length using a fade-out window. Default is True.
152
153        Notes
154        -----
155        - Uses pyfar's resample with 'freq' amplitude matching
156        - Truncation applies a right-side kaiser(8) window fade
157        - self.fs is updated to reflect the new sampling rate
158        """
159
160        if fs != self.fs:
161            self.hrirs = self._resample_save(self.hrirs, fs, truncate)
162            self.hrirs_linear = self._resample_save(self.hrirs_linear, fs, truncate)
163            self.fs = fs

def load_hp_filter(self, name, min_phase=True, n_samples=512): 
301    def load_hp_filter(self, name, min_phase=True, n_samples=512):
302        """
303        Load a headphone compensation filter by name and apply it to current HRIRs.
304        
305        Parameters
306        -------------
307        name : str
308            Subdirectory name under Headphones identifying the headphone.
309        min_phase : bool, optional
310            A boolean telling the function to use minimum phase conversion of the headphone filter. If true, 
311            the filter will be converted to minimum phase, resulting in a way shorter filter signal, and making
312            real time computation possible. By default minimum phase conversion is turned on.
313        n_samples : int, optional
314            An integer indicating the desired length of the resulting min HRIR
315
316        Returns
317        -------------
318        pyfar.Signal
319            Loaded headphone filter signal.
320
321        Notes
322        -------------------
323        Attempts to read a SOFA filter first and falls back to loading a WAV filter if needed.
324        The loaded filter is convolved with self.hrirs before returning.
325        """
326
327        if name in (None, "", "None"):
328            self.reset_hrirs()
329            self.current_filter = None
330            return None
331        
332        # do Diffuse Field Equalization as default
333        if name == "Diffuse Field Equalization":
334            self.current_filter = name
335            return self.apply_dfe()
336
337        path = self.hp_dir / name
338        if not path.exists():
339            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Headphone filter folder not found: {path}")
340
341        # load headphoen filter as WAV
342        hp_filter = pf.io.read_audio(path / "HpFilter.wav")
343        if isinstance(hp_filter, tuple):
344            hp_filter = hp_filter[0]
345        print(f"Loaded Headphone Filter {name} from wav")
346
347        # resample if needed
348        if hp_filter.sampling_rate != self.fs:
349            hp_filter = pf.dsp.resample(
350                hp_filter,
351                self.fs,
352                match_amplitude="freq",
353            )
354        
355        # apply minimum phase conversion
356        if min_phase:
357            desired_length = n_samples - self.get_IR_length(linear=True)
358            if desired_length <= 0:
359                raise ValueError(
360                    "n_samples must be larger than the linear HRIR length for minimum-phase headphone filtering."
361                )
362            # apply it before convolution to the hp_filter
363            hp_filter = pf.dsp.minimum_phase(hp_filter)
364
365            # apply a kaiser window to our filter, makin the filter 'n_samples' long
366            hp_filter = pf.dsp.time_window(hp_filter, 
367                                            (0, desired_length-1), 
368                                            window=('kaiser', 8), 
369                                            shape='right', 
370                                            crop='window')
371            
372        # apply headphone filter to hrirs
373        self.hrirs = pf.dsp.convolve(self.hrirs_linear, hp_filter, mode='full')
374        self.current_filter = name
375        return hp_filter

Load a headphone compensation filter by name and apply it to current HRIRs.

Parameters

  • min_phase (bool, optional): A boolean telling the function to use minimum phase conversion of the headphone filter. If true, the filter will be converted to minimum phase, resulting in a way shorter filter signal, and making real time computation possible. By default minimum phase conversion is turned on.
  • n_samples (int, optional): An integer indicating the desired length of the resulting min HRIR
Returns
