def apply_dfe(self): 
393    def apply_dfe(self):
394        """
395        Apply Diffuse Field Equalization (DFE) to the HRIRs.
396        
397        Computes a minimum-phase DFE filter by averaging all HRIRs, inverting
398        the average response, and convolving the result with the original
399        unmodified HRIRs. This equalizes frequency-response variations across
400        directions.
401
402        Returns
403        -------
404        pf.Signal
405            The minimum-phase DFE filter applied to self.hrirs_linear.
406
407        Notes
408        -----
409        - Uses regularized spectrum inversion with frequency range [50 Hz, 16 kHz]
410        - Sets self.hrirs to the equalized result
411        - DFE is a standard preprocessing for improved binaural quality
412        - Computation may be slow for large HRTF datasets
413        """
414        # averaging each HRTF with the average of all HRTF
415        average = pf.dsp.average(self.hrirs_linear, mode='power',caxis=0)
416        # Inversion
417        regularized = pf.dsp.RegularizedSpectrumInversion.from_frequency_range(
418            average, [50, 16e3], beta='max')
419        inverted = regularized.invert
420        # minimum phase
421        min_phase_dfe = pf.dsp.minimum_phase(inverted, truncate=False)
422
423        # convolve hrirs with the dfe filter
424        self.hrirs = pf.dsp.convolve(self.hrirs_linear, min_phase_dfe, mode='full')
425
426        return min_phase_dfe

Apply Diffuse Field Equalization (DFE) to the HRIRs.

Computes a minimum-phase DFE filter by averaging all HRIRs, inverting the average response, and convolving the result with the original unmodified HRIRs. This equalizes frequency-response variations across directions.

Returns
  • pf.Signal: The minimum-phase DFE filter applied to self.hrirs_linear.
Notes
  • Uses regularized spectrum inversion with frequency range [50 Hz, 16 kHz]
  • Sets self.hrirs to the equalized result
  • DFE is a standard preprocessing for improved binaural quality
  • Computation may be slow for large HRTF datasets

432    def __init__(self):
433        """
434        Initialize an HRTF preprocessing controller.
435        
436        Sets up the available preprocessing algorithms (LS, MagLS, TA, BiMagLS)
437        and algorithm-specific gain factors for binaural rendering.
438
439        Attributes

442            Supported preprocessing algorithm names.
443        current_algorithm : str
444            Name of the currently active algorithm. Default is 'LS'.
445        _gain : dict
446            Algorithm-specific pre-gain multipliers (e.g., MagLS requires 1.28).
447        """
448
449        # the different algorithms available
450        self.algorithms = ['LS', 'MagLS', 'TA', 'BiMagLS']
451        # the current algorithm
452        self.current_algorithm = 'LS'
453        # for each algorithm, a different pre-gain might be necessary.
454        self._gain = {
455            'LS': 1., 
456            'MagLS': 1.28, 
457            'TA': 1., 
458            'BiMagLS': 1.28
459        }
460
461    def get_gain(self):
462        """
463        Return the pre-gain factor for the currently selected preprocessing algorithm.
464        
465        Returns
466        ----------
467        float
468            Algorithm-specific pre-gain multiplier.
469        """
470
471        return self._gain[self.current_algorithm]
472
473    # apply the chosen preprocessing algorithm. use MagLS as default
474    def apply_preprocessing(self, hrirs, sh, algorithm='LS'):
475        """
476        Apply the selected preprocessing algorithm to HRIRs and return SH-domain data.
477        
478        Parameters
479        -----------
480        hrirs : pyfar.Signal
481            Time-domain HRIRs.
482        sh : spharpy.SphericalHarmonics
483            Spherical-harmonic providing the basis matrix.
484        algorithm : str, optional
485            Algorithm identifier ('LS', 'MagLS', 'TA', 'BiMagLS'). Default 'LS'.
486
487        Returns
488        ------------
489        pyfar.Signal
490            Spherical-harmonic coefficients.
491        """
492
493        match algorithm:
494            case 'LS':
495                print("Using standard spherical harmonics processing (Least Squares): Simple matrix multiplication.")
496                self.current_algorithm = algorithm
497                return self.__ls(hrirs, sh)
498            case 'MagLS':
499                print("Using MagLS HRTF Preprocessing")
500                self.current_algorithm = algorithm
501                return self.__mag_ls(hrirs, sh)
502            case 'TA':
503                print("TA not implemented yet. Falling back to MagLS/LS preprocessing.")
504                return self.apply_preprocessing(hrirs, sh, algorithm='MagLS')
505            case 'BiMagLS':
506                print("BiMagLS not implemented yet. Falling back to MagLS/LS preprocessing.")
507                return self.apply_preprocessing(hrirs, sh, algorithm='MagLS')
508            case _:
509                print("Unknown preprocessing algorithm. Using LS preprocessing.")
510                self.current_algorithm = 'LS'
511                return self.__ls(hrirs, sh)
512
513    # solves the Least Squares Problem. This means just applying the spherical Harmonics to the HRTF
514    def __ls(self, hrirs: pf.Signal, sh: spharpy.SphericalHarmonics):
515        """
516        Compute spherical-harmonic coefficients via least-squares inversion.
517        
518        Applies the inverse spherical-harmonic basis matrix directly to the
519        HRIRs via matrix multiplication: h_nm = sh.basis_inv @ hrirs.
520
521        Parameters
522        ----------
523        hrirs : pf.Signal
524            Time-domain HRIR data.
525        sh : spharpy.SphericalHarmonics
526            Spherical-harmonic object containing the basis matrix.
527
528        Returns
529        -------
530        pf.Signal
531            Spherical-harmonic coefficients with shape (n_directions, n_channels, n_samples).
532
533        Notes
534        -----
535        - Direct, fast approach; no iterative optimization
536        - Used for low SH orders or as fallback when MagLS fails
537        - Can produce phase artifacts at low orders; consider MagLS for perceptual quality
538        """
539
540        return (sh.basis_inv @ hrirs).T
541
542    # apply the magnitude least squares algorithm for better results for low order ambisonics
543    # ramp = 0 -> no ramp. ramp = 1 -> default ramp (cutoff * (1/sqrt(2))). ramp > 1 -> specific ramp in freq
544    def __mag_ls(self, hrirs: pf.Signal, sh: spharpy.SphericalHarmonics, cutoff=3000, ramp=1):
545        """
546        Compute Magnitude-Least-Squares spherical-harmonic coefficients with optional ramping.
547        
548        Parameters
549        -------------
550        hrirs : pyfar.Signal
551            HRIR data (time or freq representation used internally).
552        sh : spharpy.SphericalHarmonics
553            Spherical-harmonic providing basis matrix.
554        cutoff : float, optional
555            Frequency (Hz) above which magnitude-only optimization is applied.
556        ramp : float or bool, optional
557            If > 0, apply a smooth ramp before cutoff frequency; if 1 use a 
558            default width of cutoff * (1 / sqrt(2)).
559
560        Returns
561        -----------
562        pyfar.Signal
563            pyfar Signal containing spherical-harmonic coefficients converted back to time domain.
564
565        Notes
566        ------------
567        This function performs per-frequency optimization and is computationally heavier than LS.
568        """
569        # make our data frequency data
570        hrirs_freq = hrirs.freq_raw.copy()
571        # find corresponding frequency bin
572        freq_axis = hrirs.frequencies
573        stop = hrirs.find_nearest_frequency(cutoff)
574
575        # create alpha value for each frequency: possibly with a ramp up? or just 0/1?
576        # with just 0/1 we might have to smooth the phase later
577        alpha = np.zeros_like(freq_axis, dtype=float)
578        alpha[stop:] = 1
579        start = stop
580
581        # make a ramp up if needed. Use Hanning for smoothness
582        if ramp > 0:
583            # use default ramp of f * (1/sqrt(2))
584            if ramp == 1:
585                ramp = cutoff * (1 / np.sqrt(2))
586            # find start and stop indices. find_nearest_freq should always return valid indices
587            start = hrirs.find_nearest_frequency(cutoff - ramp)
588            stop = hrirs.find_nearest_frequency(cutoff)
589            length = max(stop - start, 0)
590            # create a Hanning window, use the half that goes from 0 -> 1
591            win = np.hanning(2*length)[:length]
592            alpha[start:start+length] = win
593
594        # below cutoff: do simple least squares
595        # do regular  least squares -> simple matrix mult
596        hrirs_sh = self.__ls(hrirs, sh).freq_raw
597        nm_magls = hrirs_sh.copy()
598        sh_basis = sh.basis.copy()
599
600        # for each ear, for each frequency, starting at the cutoff bin
601        for ear in range(2):
602            for f in range(start, freq_axis.size):
603                # for each ear, all directional data, and the current frequency: find magls
604                # solve the magnitude only optimization
605                # above cutoff: do least squares, magnitude from original, phase from min-phase
606                nm_magls[ear, :, f] = (
607                    # use shroom library for speed
608                    alpha[f] * sh_util.magls(A=sh_basis, 
609                                             b=hrirs_freq[:, ear, f], 
610                                             x_prev=nm_magls[ear, :, f-1]
611                                             )
612                    + (1 - alpha[f]) * hrirs_sh[ear, :, f]
613                )
614        
615        # create time domain by creating a pyfar Signal from frequency data
616        hrirs_sh_time = pf.Signal(nm_magls, hrirs.sampling_rate, n_samples=hrirs.n_samples, domain='freq')
617        return hrirs_sh_time

class SphericalHarmonics: 
  19class SphericalHarmonics:
  20    """
  21    Real-time binaural renderer using spherical-harmonic HRTF decomposition.
  22
  23    This class manages the complete pipeline for head-tracked binaural audio:
  24    loads an HRTF dataset, decomposes HRIRs into spherical-harmonic coefficients,
  25    performs head-rotation transformations via Wigner-D matrices, and applies
  26    fast frequency-domain convolution with overlap-add buffering and smooth
  27    crossfading during rotation transitions.
  28
  29    Parameters
  30    ----------
  31    hrtf : HRTF or None, optional
  32        Preloaded HRTF instance. If None, the default FABIAN HRTF is loaded.
  33        Default is None.
  34    sampling_rate : int or float, optional
  35        Target sampling rate in Hz. HRTF resampling is automatic if needed.
  36        Default is 44100.
  37    ambi_order : int, optional
  38        Ambisonic order (0–7) for spherical-harmonic decomposition.
  39        Default is 1 (first-order).
  40    preprocess : str, optional
  41        Preprocessing algorithm: 'LS' (Least Squares), 'MagLS' (recommended),
  42        'TA', or 'BiMagLS'. Default is 'MagLS'.
  43    block_size : int, optional
  44        Audio block size in samples. If None, auto-set to next power of two
  45        greater than IR length. Default is None.
  46
  47    Attributes
  48    ----------
  49    hrtf : HRTF
  50        Loaded HRTF dataset instance.
  51    sampling_rate : int
  52        Current sampling rate in Hz.
  53    ambi_order : int
  54        Current Ambisonic order.
  55    sources : spharpy.SamplingSphere
  56        HRTF spatial sampling grid.
  57    hrir_nm : np.ndarray
  58        Spherical-harmonic HRIR coefficients (time domain).
  59        Shape: (2, n_sh_channels, n_samples).
  60    hrir_nm_fft : np.ndarray
  61        Zero-padded FFT of spherical-harmonic HRIRs for convolution.
  62        Shape: (2, n_sh_channels, n_freq_bins).
  63    hrir_nm_rot : dict
  64        Current and previous rotated SH-HRIR spectra with keys 'old' and 'new'.
  65    block_size : int
  66        Audio processing block size in samples.
  67    N : int
  68        FFT length for overlap-add (>= block_size + IR_length - 1).
  69    overlap_buffer : np.ndarray
  70        Tail from last block for overlap-add continuity. Shape: (IR_length-1, 2).
  71    overlap_buffer_old : np.ndarray
  72        Tail from previous rotation filter during crossfade.
  73    pre_gain : float
  74        Output gain multiplier (default 0.1).
  75    atol : float
  76        Rotation tolerance in radians for skipping negligible updates (default ≈ 1°).
  77
  78    Notes
  79    -----
  80    - A daemon thread manages asynchronous rotation updates (see _rotation_worker)
  81    - Uses SN3D normalization and real spherical harmonics (AmbiX convention)
  82    - Crossfade ramp: 32-sample equal-power sine² curve
  83    - Call close() before object destruction to cleanly terminate the rotation thread
  84    - Thread-safe rotation updates via queue and locks
  85    - Supports smooth head-rotation transitions with zero audio clicks
  86
  87    Examples
  88    --------
  89    >>> sh = SphericalHarmonics(ambi_order=3, sampling_rate=48000)
  90    >>> for chunk in ambi_stream:
  91    ...     sh.set_rotation([yaw, pitch, roll])  # Non-blocking queue
  92    ...     output = sh.process_ola_rot(chunk)
  93    ...     play(output)
  94    >>> sh.close()
  95    """
  96
  97    # Constructor
  98    def __init__(self, hrtf: HRTF = None, sampling_rate=44_100, ambi_order=1, preprocess='MagLS', block_size=None):
  99        """
 100        Initialize spherical-harmonic HRTF processing and convolution engine.
 101        
 102        This constructor loads or receives an HRTF dataset, converts HRIRs to
 103        spherical-harmonic coefficients for the given Ambisonic order, and
 104        initializes the real-time convolution pipeline with overlap-add buffers,
 105        rotation matrices, and a background rotation worker thread. This call is
 106        blocking and may take considerable time (typically several seconds).
 107
 108        Parameters
 109        ----------
 110        hrtf : HRTF or None, optional
 111            Preloaded HRTF instance. If None, the default FABIAN HRTF dataset
 112            is downloaded and loaded. Default is None.
 113        sampling_rate : int or float, optional
 114            Target sampling rate in Hz for HRIR resampling. The HRTF will be
 115            resampled if its native sampling rate differs. Default is 44100.
 116        ambi_order : int, optional
 117            Ambisonic order (0, 1, 2, ..., 7) for spherical-harmonic 
 118            decomposition. Higher orders require more computation but provide
 119            better directional accuracy. Default is 1 (first-order Ambisonics).
 120        preprocess : str, optional
 121            Preprocessing algorithm for HRTF conversion. Currently supported:
 122            'LS' (Least Squares), 'MagLS' (Magnitude Least Squares, recommended),
 123            'TA' (not yet implemented), 'BiMagLS' (not yet implemented).
 124            Default is 'MagLS'.
 125        block_size : int, optional
 126            Audio processing block size in samples. Must match the buffer size
 127            used in real-time playback for correct overlap-add convolution.
 128            If None, automatically set to the next power of two greater than
 129            the HRIR length. Default is None.
 130
 131        Attributes
 132        ----------
 133        hrtf : HRTF
 134            Loaded HRTF instance.
 135        sampling_rate : int
 136            Current sampling rate in Hz.
 137        ambi_order : int
 138            Current Ambisonic order.
 139        sources : spharpy.SamplingSphere
 140            Spatial sampling points of the HRTF measurement directions.
 141        hrir_nm : np.ndarray
 142            Spherical-harmonic coefficients of HRIRs in time domain.
 143        hrir_nm_fft : np.ndarray
 144            FFT of zero-padded spherical-harmonic HRIRs (for convolution).
 145        hrir_nm_rot : dict
 146            Current rotated SH-HRIRs in frequency domain with keys 'old' and 'new'.
 147        block_size : int
 148            Audio processing block size in samples.
 149        N : int
 150            FFT length for overlap-add (>= block_size + IR_length - 1).
 151        overlap_buffer : np.ndarray
 152            Tail samples from last convolution (shape: (IR_length-1, 2)).
 153        overlap_buffer_old : np.ndarray
 154            Tail samples from previous rotation filter state.
 155        pre_gain : float
 156            Overall gain factor applied to all output (default 0.1).
 157
 158        Raises
 159        ------
 160        Exception
 161            If HRTF loading (from file and web) both fail.
 162
 163        Notes
 164        -----
 165        - A daemon thread (_rotation_worker) is started for asynchronous head
 166        rotation updates; terminate via close() before object destruction
 167        - Uses SN3D normalization and real spherical harmonics (AmbiX convention)
 168        - Crossfade ramp length is fixed at 32 samples by default
 169        - Default tolerance for rotation changes: 1 degree (radians)
 170        - Equal-power sine-squared ramps ensure smooth audio during transitions
 171        """
 172        start = time.time()
 173        
 174        # # set the hrtf. this should be a pyfar signal!
 175        # self.hrtf = hrtf
 176
 177        # set sample rate. we should make sure this is the same as for the HRTFs!!!
 178        self.sampling_rate = sampling_rate
 179
 180        if hrtf == None:
 181            # load FABIAN from the web if no HRTF was given
 182            self.hrtf = HRTF()
 183        else:
 184            self.hrtf = hrtf
 185
 186        # make sure the sampling rate is correct and resample if necessary
 187        if self.hrtf.fs != sampling_rate:
 188            self.hrtf.resample(sampling_rate)
 189
 190        # store the sources in a Sampling Sphere
 191        self.sources = sh.SamplingSphere.from_coordinates(self.hrtf.sources)
 192
 193        # create a spherical harmonics definition, corresponding to the AmbiX convention
 194        self.ambi_order = ambi_order
 195        self.sh_definition = sh.SphericalHarmonicDefinition(self.ambi_order, 
 196                                                            normalization="SN3D", 
 197                                                            basis_type='real', 
 198                                                            condon_shortley=False
 199                                                            )
 200
 201        # create the spherical harmonics object from definition and sampling sphere
 202        self.spherical_harmonics = sh.SphericalHarmonics.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
 203                                                                         self.sources, 
 204                                                                        #  inverse_method="pseudo_inverse"
 205                                                                         )
 206
 207        # create hrtf processing unit
 208        self.process = Processing()
 209
 210        # create h_nm matrix 
 211        hrirs_nm = self.process.apply_preprocessing(self.hrtf.hrirs, 
 212                                               self.spherical_harmonics,
 213                                               algorithm=preprocess
 214                                               )
 215        
 216        print("Convert to Spherical Harmonic Signal")
 217        self.hrir_nm = sh.SphericalHarmonicSignal.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
 218                                                                   hrirs_nm.time, 
 219                                                                   hrirs_nm.sampling_rate
 220                                                                   ).time
 221        
 222        *_, pad_to_length = self.hrir_nm.shape
 223
 224        # update this later by calling update_hrirs_fft() once we know the desired fft length
 225        self.hrir_nm_fft = np.fft.fft(self.hrir_nm, next_power_of_two(pad_to_length), axis=-1)
 226
 227        # create SH rotation unit
 228        self.rotation = RotationMatrix()
 229        # prepare rotated hrir's, and our rotation matrix, with all angles 0 currently
 230        self.hrir_nm_rot = {
 231                           'old' : self.hrir_nm_fft.copy(),
 232                           'new' : self.hrir_nm_fft.copy()
 233                           }
 234        self._D = {
 235                  'old' : np.eye(order_to_channel_n(ambi_order)),
 236                  'new' : np.eye(order_to_channel_n(ambi_order))
 237                  }
 238        self._last_rotation = Rotation.from_euler('zyx', (0, 0, 0))
 239        self.atol = np.deg2rad(1)
 240
 241        self._rotation_lock = threading.Lock()
 242        self._rotation_queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=1)
 243        self._rotation_update = threading.Event()
 244        self._stop_rotation_thread = threading.Event()
 245
 246        # start the rotation thread
 247        self._rotation_thread = threading.Thread(
 248            target=self._rotation_worker,
 249            daemon=True,
 250        )
 251        self._rotation_thread.start()
 252
 253        # States for overlap-add (must be reset on seek)
 254        self.overlap_buffer = np.zeros((self.get_IR_length() - 1, 2), dtype=np.float32)
 255        self.overlap_buffer_old = np.zeros_like(self.overlap_buffer)
 256        self.interpolate_rot = None
 257        # overlap add L = self.get_IR_length()
 258        if block_size is None:
 259            block_size = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length())
 260        self.block_size = block_size
 261        # overlap add N
 262        # compute N >= M + L - 1
 263        self.N = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length() + block_size - 1)
 264
 265        # prepare ramp for crossfading between rotations
 266        self._cf_flag = 0
 267        self._set_crossfade_length(32)
 268
 269        # use this function because we will not calculate D otherwise
 270        self.update_rotation_matrix([0, 0, 0])
 271
 272        # prepare pre_gain for gianstaging
 273        self.pre_gain = 0.1
 274        print(f"Setting up Spherical Harmonics took {time.time() - start:.2f}s")
 275
 276    def update_order(self, order: int, block_size=None):
 277        """
 278        Update the Ambisonic order and recompute all spherical-harmonic components.
 279        
 280        This method recalculates the spherical-harmonic basis, performs preprocessing
 281        on the HRIRs for the new order, and updates all internal FFT buffers and 
 282        rotation matrices. This call is blocking and may take considerable time.
 283
 284        Parameters
 285        ----------
 286        order : int
 287            New Ambisonic order for spherical-harmonic decomposition.
 288        block_size : int, optional
 289            Audio processing block size in samples. If None, automatically computed 
 290            as the next power of two greater than IR length. Default is None.
 291
 292        Raises
 293        ------
 294        ValueError
 295            If order is negative.
 296        """
 297        # create a spherical harmonics definition, corresponding to the AmbiX convention
 298        self.ambi_order = order
 299        self.sh_definition = sh.SphericalHarmonicDefinition(self.ambi_order, 
 300                                                            normalization="SN3D", 
 301                                                            basis_type='real', 
 302                                                            condon_shortley=False
 303                                                            )
 304
 305        # create the spherical harmonics object from definition and sampling sphere
 306        self.spherical_harmonics = sh.SphericalHarmonics.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
 307                                                                         self.sources, 
 308                                                                         inverse_method="pseudo_inverse"
 309                                                                         )
 310        # create h_nm matrix 
 311        hrirs_nm = self.process.apply_preprocessing(self.hrtf.hrirs, 
 312                                               self.spherical_harmonics,
 313                                               algorithm='MagLS'
 314                                               )
 315        
 316        # update our hrir_nm
 317        self.hrir_nm = sh.SphericalHarmonicSignal.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
 318                                                                   hrirs_nm.time, 
 319                                                                   hrirs_nm.sampling_rate
 320                                                                   ).time
 321        
 322        # prepare hrir_nm_fft
 323        if block_size is None:
 324            block_size = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length())
 325        # this calls update_hrirs_fft internally!
 326        self.update_process_variables(block_size)
 327        
 328    
 329    def update_process_variables(self, block_size: int):
 330        """
 331        Updated the variables necessary to perform successfull Overlap-Add algorithm on processing.
 332
 333        Parameters
 334        ----------
 335        block_size : int
 336            The buffer size we are currently working with
 337        """
 338        self.block_size = block_size
 339        # compute N >= M + L - 1
 340        self.N = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length() + block_size - 1)
 341
 342        # update our sh fft coefficients once (and on each rotation update)
 343        self.update_hrirs_fft(self.N)
 344        self.update_rotation_matrix(self._last_rotation.as_euler('zyx', degrees=True))
 345
 346        self._set_crossfade_length(32)
 347        self._ramp = hanning_ramp(self._cf_length, 2)
 348        # allocate buffers
 349        self.overlap_buffer = np.zeros((self.get_IR_length() - 1, 2), dtype=np.float32)
 350        self.overlap_buffer_old = np.zeros_like(self.overlap_buffer)
 351
 352    def get_IR_length(self):
 353        """
 354        Return the impulse-response length (number of samples) of the current HRIRs.
 355
 356        Returns
 357        -----------
 358        int
 359            Number of samples in the HRIR time-domain representation.
 360        """
 361        *_, n_samples = self.hrir_nm.shape
 362        return n_samples
 363    
 364    def restart_rotation(self):
 365        """
 366        Terminate the current rotation thread and start a new one.
 367        
 368        This method safely closes any existing rotation worker thread, clears
 369        synchronization flags, and spawns a fresh daemon thread. Use this after
 370        major configuration changes or when rotation state needs to be reset.
 371
 372        Raises
 373        ------
 374        Exception
 375            If the existing rotation thread cannot be terminated within 1 second.
 376        """
 377        # close old rotation thread if it exists and is alive
 378        if self._rotation_thread is not None:
 379            if self._rotation_thread.is_alive():
 380                # set the stop flag, set rotation update and hope old thread will close
 381                self._stop_rotation_thread.set()
 382                self._rotation_update.set()
 383                self._rotation_thread.join(1.)
 384                if self._rotation_thread.is_alive():
 385                    raise Exception("Couldn't close rotation thread.")
 386                
 387            self._rotation_thread = None
 388
 389        # clear the stop and rotation flag
 390        self._stop_rotation_thread.clear()
 391        self._rotation_update.clear()
 392        # start a new rotation thread
 393        self._rotation_thread = threading.Thread(
 394            target=self._rotation_worker,
 395            daemon=True,
 396        )
 397        self._rotation_thread.start()
 398
 399    def update_rotation_matrix(self, angles, convention='zyx'):
 400        """
 401        Directly Compute and update the internal Wigner-D matrix based on thie given Euler angles in degrees (zyx). This will block the thread!
 402        The updating is done in a thread-safe manner.
 403
 404        Parameters
 405        ----------
 406        angles : sequence of float
 407            Euler angles in degrees as (z, y, x).
 408        convention : str
 409            A string identifying the used convention/order of the angles. 'zyx' is default.
 410        """
 411        rotation = Rotation.from_euler(convention, angles, degrees=True)
 412        alpha, beta, gamma = rotation.as_euler("zyz")
 413        new_D = self.rotation.real_wigner_d_matrix(self.ambi_order, alpha, beta, gamma)
 414
 415         # using the fft, since we expect this to be faster than time domain
 416        # 3. Apply rotation
 417        # data is (Channels, SH, Time/Freq)
 418        # D is (SH, SH)
 419        # We want D @ data
 420        # einsum: ij, cjk -> cik
 421        # self.hrir_nm_rot = np.einsum("ij, cjk -> cik", self.D, hrir_rot)
 422        new_rot = new_D @ self.hrir_nm_fft
 423        with self._rotation_lock:
 424            self._D['old'] = self._D['new'].copy()
 425            self._D['new'] = new_D
 426            self.hrir_nm_rot['old'] = self.hrir_nm_rot['new'].copy()
 427            self.hrir_nm_rot['new'] = new_rot
 428
 429            # also swap old OLA buffer. new one gets updated in OLA logic
 430            # self.overlap_buffer_old = self.overlap_buffer.copy()
 431            # self.overlap_buffer[:] = 0.0
 432
 433            # a crossfade needs to happen now!
 434            self._cf_flag = 1
 435            self._cf_pos = 0
 436
 437    def set_rotation(self, angles, convention='zyx'):
 438        """
 439        Compute and update the internal Wigner-D matrix based on thie given Euler angles in degrees (zyx) by passing it to the worker thread.
 440        The updating is done in a thread-safe manner.
 441
 442        Parameters
 443        ----------
 444        angles : sequence of float
 445            Euler angles in degrees as (z, y, x).
 446        convention : str
 447            A string identifying the used convention/order of the angles. 'zyx' is default.
 448        """
 449        try:
 450            self._rotation_queue.put_nowait((angles, convention))
 451        except queue.Full:
 452            try:
 453                # drop the last cached block. queue should be empty now, since we only have size 1
 454                self._rotation_queue.get_nowait()
 455                print("Queue is already full! Dropping this rotation update")
 456            except queue.Empty:
 457                pass
 458            # try putting a new block into the queue again after draining it
 459            self._rotation_queue.put_nowait((angles, convention))
 460
 461        # finally, set the flag if we managed to successfully set a rotation
 462        self._rotation_update.set()
 463
 464    def _rotation_worker(self):
 465        """
 466        Worker thread for asynchronous Wigner-D matrix updates.
 467        
 468        This method runs continuously in a separate daemon thread, waiting for
 469        rotation update requests from the queue. When a rotation is received,
 470        it computes the real Wigner-D matrix, applies it to the frequency-domain
 471        HRIRs, and updates the filter state in a thread-safe manner with proper
 472        synchronization for crossfade transitions.
 473
 474        Notes
 475        -----
 476        - Runs as a daemon thread started in __init__
 477        - Monitors self._rotation_update event and self._stop_rotation_thread flag
 478        - Skips negligible rotations (< self.atol tolerance)
 479        - Triggers crossfade when filter state changes via self._cf_flag
 480        """
 481        while not self._stop_rotation_thread.is_set():
 482
 483            # sleep cheaply until something happens. this blocks!
 484            self._rotation_update.wait()
 485            if self._stop_rotation_thread.is_set():
 486                break
 487            # clear the update flag and consume the current angles and convention
 488            self._rotation_update.clear()
 489
 490            # get pending angles and rotation
 491            try:
 492                angles, convention = self._rotation_queue.get_nowait()
 493            except queue.Empty:
 494                continue
 495
 496            rotation = Rotation.from_euler(convention, angles, degrees=True)
 497            # skip this calculation if no meaningful rotation has happened
 498            if rotation.approx_equal(self._last_rotation, atol=self.atol):
 499                continue
 500
 501            # compute wigner D matrix
 502            alpha, beta, gamma = rotation.as_euler("zyz")
 503            new_D = self.rotation.real_wigner_d_matrix(self.ambi_order, alpha, beta, gamma)
 504    
 505            # using the fft, since we expect this to be faster than time domain
 506            # 3. Apply rotation
 507            # data is (Channels, SH, Time/Freq)
 508            # D is (SH, SH)
 509            # We want D @ data
 510            # einsum: ij, cjk -> cik
 511            # self.hrir_nm_rot = np.einsum("ij, cjk -> cik", self.D, hrir_rot)
 512            new_rot = new_D @ self.hrir_nm_fft
 513            with self._rotation_lock:
 514                self._D['old'] = self._D['new'].copy()
 515                self._D['new'] = new_D
 516                self.hrir_nm_rot['old'] = self.hrir_nm_rot['new'].copy()
 517                self.hrir_nm_rot['new'] = new_rot
 518
 519                # interpolate
 520                # self.interpolate_rot = self.interpolate(self._last_rotation, rotation, block_size=self._cf_length)
 521
 522                # # also swap old OLA buffer. new one gets updated in OLA logic
 523                # self.overlap_buffer_old = self.overlap_buffer.copy()
 524                # self.overlap_buffer[:] = 0.0
 525
 526                # a crossfade needs to happen now!
 527                self._cf_flag = 1
 528                self._cf_pos = 0
 529
 530            # update the last rotation
 531            self._last_rotation = rotation
 532
 533    def get_rotation_matrix(self):
 534        """
 535        Return a copy of the currently stored Wigner-D rotation matrices.
 536        
 537        Retrieves both the 'old' and 'new' Wigner-D matrices in a thread-safe
 538        manner (holding the rotation lock). This allows safe access to the
 539        current and previous filter rotations during interpolation.
 540
 541        Returns
 542        -------
 543        dict or None
 544            Dictionary with keys 'old' and 'new', each containing a Wigner-D
 545            matrix of shape ((order+1)^2, (order+1)^2). Returns None if no
 546            rotation matrix is available.
 547        """
 548        with self._rotation_lock:
 549            if self._D is None:
 550                return None
 551            
 552            return self._D.copy()
 553
 554    # set the current rotation angle
 555    def _apply_rotation(self):
 556        """
 557        Apply rotation matrices to the frequency-domain HRIR coefficients.
 558        
 559        Multiplies the zero-padded frequency-domain spherical-harmonic HRIRs
 560        by the current and previous (for crossfade) Wigner-D rotation matrices
 561        using efficient matrix-vector products. Updates self.hrir_nm_rot['old']
 562        and self.hrir_nm_rot['new'].
 563
 564        Notes
 565        -----
 566        - Operates in frequency domain (self.hrir_nm_fft already zero-padded)
 567        - Matrix operation: (SH channels, SH order, FFT bins)
 568        - Used internally during overlap-add processing
 569        - Thread-safe via rotation lock
 570        """
 571        # using the fft, since we expect this to be faster than time domain
 572        # 3. Apply rotation
 573        # data is (Channels, SH, Time/Freq)
 574        # D is (SH, SH)
 575        # We want D @ data
 576        # einsum: ij, cjk -> cik
 577        # self.hrir_nm_rot = np.einsum("ij, cjk -> cik", self.D, hrir_rot)
 578        D = self.get_rotation_matrix()
 579        # if D is None, do nothing and keep our latest rotated hrir_nm
 580        if D is not None:
 581            # using the fft, since we expect this to be faster than time domain
 582            self.hrir_nm_rot['old'] = D['old'] @ self.hrir_nm_fft
 583            self.hrir_nm_rot['new'] = D['new'] @ self.hrir_nm_fft
 584    
 585    # apply the hrtf data to an ambisonics file
 586    def apply_hrtf_full(self, ambi_signal: pf.Signal, gain=1.):
 587        """
 588        Convolve an ambisonic signal with the rotated HRTFs to produce a stereo signal.
 589
 590        Parameters
 591        ----------
 592        ambi_signal : pyfar.Signal
 593            Ambisonic input signal (should have cshape (n_channels,)).
 594        gain : float, optional
 595            A float between 0. and 1., applied after internal gain-staging, Default is 1.
 596
 597        Returns
 598        -------
 599        numpy.ndarray
 600            Stereo time-domain array with shape (2, n_samples) containing left and right channels.
 601
 602        Raises
 603        -----------
 604        AttributeError
 605            If gain is outside [0., 1.].
 606        ValueError
 607            If Ambisonic channel count mismatches the HRTF channels.
 608        """
 609
 610        if gain > 1. or gain < 0:
 611            raise AttributeError("The gain must be in range [0., 1.].")
 612
 613        # apply rotation to the sh_hrir
 614        sh_hrir = self.hrir_nm.copy()
 615
 616        # Check channel count by comparing the channel shape
 617        # we know the channel shape for ambi_signal is (channels,)
 618        ambi_ch, *_ = ambi_signal.cshape
 619        # we know the channel shape for sh_hrir is (2, channels)
 620        _, sh_hrir_ch, _ = sh_hrir.shape
 621        if ambi_ch != sh_hrir_ch:
 622            raise ValueError("Channel counts must match (16 for 3rd order).")
 623
 624        # create our time signals
 625        left = sh_hrir[0, :, :]
 626        right = sh_hrir[1, :, :]
 627
 628        # sh_hrir should have the shape (2, ambi_order)
 629        # Convolve each channel separately for left and right
 630        # instantly store it as time data
 631        left_conv = pf.dsp.convolve(
 632            ambi_signal,
 633            pf.Signal(left, 
 634                      self.sampling_rate, 
 635                      domain='time'
 636                      ), # need to get the left channel here
 637            mode='full',
 638            method='overlap_add'
 639        ).time
 640        right_conv = pf.dsp.convolve(
 641            ambi_signal,
 642            pf.Signal(right, 
 643                      self.sampling_rate, 
 644                      domain='time'
 645                      ), # need to get the right channel here
 646            mode='full',
 647            method='overlap_add'
 648        ).time
 649
 650        # Sum over channels -> single‑channel binaural signals
 651        left_signal = np.sum(left_conv, axis=0)
 652        right_signal = np.sum(right_conv, axis=0)
 653
 654        # do gain staging
 655        left_signal *= self.pre_gain * gain
 656        right_signal *= self.pre_gain * gain
 657        # possibly make a clipping warning
 658        self.test_clipping([left_signal, right_signal])
 659
 660        # create stereo signal by stacking the time data horizontally
 661        stereo_time = np.vstack((left_signal, right_signal))
 662        # stereo = pf.Signal(stereo_time, 
 663        #                    sampling_rate=self.sampling_rate, 
 664        #                    domain='time'
 665        #                    )
 666
 667        return stereo_time
 668    
 669    # apply the hrtf data to an ambisonics file
 670    def apply_hrtf_chunk(self, ambi_signal: np.ndarray, block_size=1024):
 671        """
 672        Convolve an ambisonic signal with the rotated HRTFs in the frequency domain to produce a stereo signal.
 673        This function expects a signal as NDarray, as well as a blocksize to operate on (must fit the blocksize of `self.hrir_nm_rot`)
 674
 675        Parameters
 676        ----------
 677        ambi_signal : np.ndarray
 678            Input block or stream (should have shape (n_samples, n_channels)).
 679        block_size : int, optional
 680            FFT size / processing block length. Default 1024.
 681        gain : float, optional
 682            A float between 0. and 1., applied after internal gain-staging, Default is 1.
 683
 684        Returns
 685        -------
 686        numpy.ndarray
 687            Stereo time-domain array (n_samples, 2) after convolution and gain staging.
 688
 689        Notes
 690        -------------
 691        Assumes self.hrirs_nm_fft has been prepared via update_hrirs_fft(block_size).
 692        """
 693    
 694        # checking of channel count should be done elsewhere
 695        # check for correct gain also elsewhere!
 696
 697        # apply rotation to the sh_hrir
 698        # not needed, we only apply rotation and update hrir_nm_rot on a new rotation
 699        # self._apply_rotation()
 700
 701        # sh_hrir should have the shape (2, ambi_channels, n bins)
 702        #fft_sh = np.fft.fft(self.hrirs_nm, n=block_size, axis=-1)
 703
 704        # make fft of our ambi signal. shape (n_samples, n_channels)
 705        fft_ambi = np.fft.fft(ambi_signal, n=block_size, axis=0)
 706
 707        # convolve by multiplication in time domain over all channels, for each ear
 708        fft_sum = np.ndarray((2, block_size), dtype=np.complex64)
 709
 710        with self._rotation_lock:
 711            hrir_new = self.hrir_nm_rot['new'].copy()
 712
 713        for ear in range(2):
 714                # perform convolution in rotated frequency domain and sum in frequency domain
 715                fft_sum[ear] = np.sum(fft_ambi.T * hrir_new[ear, :, :], axis=0)
 716
 717        # Sum over channels -> single‑channel binaural signals
 718        sum_conv = np.fft.ifft(fft_sum).real
 719
 720        # do gain staging
 721        sum_conv *= self.pre_gain
 722        # no test for clipping because of time
 723        # transpose, since sounddevice expects shape (n_samples, n_channels)
 724        return sum_conv.T
 725    
 726    # apply the hrtf data to an ambisonics file
 727    def apply_hrtf_chunk_rot(self, ambi_signal: np.ndarray, block_size=1024):
 728        """
 729        Convolve an Ambisonic signal chunk with rotated HRTFs for crossfade.
 730        
 731        Performs frequency-domain convolution of the input Ambisonic signal
 732        with both the old and new rotated HRTF filters, enabling smooth
 733        crossfading during head-rotation transitions. Returns both results
 734        plus a flag indicating whether a crossfade is in progress.
 735
 736        Parameters
 737        ----------
 738        ambi_signal : np.ndarray
 739            Input audio block with shape (n_samples, n_channels).
 740        block_size : int, optional
 741            FFT size / processing block length. Default 1024.
 742
 743        Returns
 744        -------
 745        tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, bool]
 746            - stereo_new : Binaural output using new rotation (n_samples, 2)
 747            - stereo_old : Binaural output using old rotation (n_samples, 2)
 748            - do_fade : Boolean flag; True if crossfade is active
 749
 750        Notes
 751        -----
 752        - Requires self.hrir_nm_fft to be pre-computed via update_hrirs_fft()
 753        - Used internally by process_ola_rot() for rotation transitions
 754        - Thread-safe snapshot of rotation matrices taken under lock
 755        """
 756    
 757        # checking of channel count should be done elsewhere
 758        # check for correct gain also elsewhere!
 759
 760        # apply rotation to the sh_hrir
 761        # not needed, we only apply rotation and update hrir_nm_rot on a new rotation
 762        # self._apply_rotation()
 763
 764        # sh_hrir should have the shape (2, ambi_channels, n bins)
 765        #fft_sh = np.fft.fft(self.hrirs_nm, n=block_size, axis=-1)
 766
 767        # make fft of our ambi signal. shape (n_samples, n_channels)
 768        fft_ambi = np.fft.fft(ambi_signal, n=block_size, axis=0)
 769
 770        # convolve by multiplication in time domain over all channels, for each ear
 771        fft_sum = np.ndarray((2, block_size), dtype=np.complex64)
 772        fft_sum_old = np.ndarray((2, block_size), dtype=np.complex64)
 773
 774        # snapshot the filters under lock
 775        with self._rotation_lock:
 776            hrir_new = self.hrir_nm_rot['new'].copy()
 777            hrir_old = self.hrir_nm_rot['old'].copy()
 778            do_fade = self._cf_flag > 0
 779
 780        for ear in range(2):
 781            # perform convolution in rotated frequency domain and sum in frequency domain
 782            # get old and new rotation resluts
 783            fft_sum[ear] = np.sum(fft_ambi.T * hrir_new[ear, :, :], axis=0)
 784            fft_sum_old[ear] = np.sum(fft_ambi.T * hrir_old[ear, :, :], axis=0)
 785
 786        sum_conv = np.fft.ifft(fft_sum).real
 787        sum_conv_old = np.fft.ifft(fft_sum_old).real
 788
 789        # do gain staging
 790        sum_conv *= self.pre_gain
 791        sum_conv_old *= self.pre_gain
 792        # no test for clipping because of time
 793        # transpose, since sounddevice expects shape (n_samples, n_channels)
 794        return sum_conv.T, sum_conv_old.T, do_fade
 795
 796    # process a single chunk of data, performing an overlap-add algorithm
 797    def process_ola(self, chunk: np.ndarray):
 798        """
 799        Process a single Ambisonic audio chunk using overlap-add convolution.
 800        
 801        Applies rotated HRTFs via frequency-domain convolution, combines with
 802        the overlap buffer from the previous chunk, and returns the valid 
 803        (non-overlapped) portion of the result. Maintains self.overlap_buffer
 804        for the next chunk.
 805
 806        Parameters
 807        ----------
 808        chunk : np.ndarray
 809            Ambisonic input block with shape (n_samples, n_channels).
 810
 811        Returns
 812        -------
 813        np.ndarray
 814            Stereo binaural output with shape (n_samples, 2), derived from 
 815            the convolution result after overlap-add.
 816
 817        Notes
 818        -----
 819        - IR length (self.get_IR_length()) must be <= block size
 820        - self.overlap_buffer is updated in-place for continuity
 821        - Does not perform crossfading; use process_ola_rot() during head rotations
 822        """
 823        # update our block size and sh_length
 824        block_size, *_ = chunk.shape
 825        sh_length = self.get_IR_length()
 826
 827        # apply hrtf
 828        # stereo = self.apply_hrtf_chunk_fft(chunk, self.N)
 829        # stereo = self.apply_hrtf_chunk_slerp(chunk, self.N)
 830        stereo = self.apply_hrtf_chunk(chunk, self.N)
 831
 832        # add overlap to stereo output
 833        stereo[:sh_length-1] += self.overlap_buffer
 834
 835        # save new overlap buffer
 836        self.overlap_buffer[:] = stereo[block_size:block_size + sh_length - 1]
 837    
 838        return stereo[:block_size]
 839
 840    def process_ola_rot(self, chunk: np.ndarray):
 841        """
 842        Process an Ambisonic chunk with overlap-add and smooth rotation crossfade.
 843        
 844        Convolves the input with both old and new rotated filters, performs
 845        separate overlap-add for each, and applies a crossfade ramp between
 846        them as the head rotation occurs. Maintains both overlap_buffer and
 847        overlap_buffer_old to support smooth transitions.
 848
 849        Parameters
 850        ----------
 851        chunk : np.ndarray
 852            Ambisonic input block with shape (n_samples, n_channels).
 853
 854        Returns
 855        -------
 856        np.ndarray
 857            Stereo binaural output with shape (n_samples, 2). During crossfade
 858            windows, this blends the old and new filter outputs.
 859
 860        Notes
 861        -----
 862        - Called during head-rotation transitions via set_rotation()
 863        - Manages self._cf_flag, self._cf_pos, and self._ramp for fade control
 864        - Thread-safe access to rotation matrices and crossfade state
 865        - Reverts to process_ola() behavior once crossfade completes
 866        """
 867
 868        # update our block size and sh_length
 869        block_size, *_ = chunk.shape
 870        sh_length = self.get_IR_length()
 871
 872        # apply hrtf
 873        stereo_new, stereo_old, do_fade = self.apply_hrtf_chunk_rot(chunk, self.N)
 874
 875        # take care of our overlap-adds before crossfading
 876        stereo_new[:sh_length-1] += self.overlap_buffer
 877        stereo_old[:sh_length-1] += self.overlap_buffer_old
 878
 879        fade_finished = not do_fade
 880
 881        if do_fade:
 882            with self._rotation_lock:
 883                # do crossfade
 884                fade_start = self._cf_pos
 885                fade_end = min(fade_start + block_size, self._cf_length)
 886                fade_n = max(0, fade_end - fade_start)
 887
 888            if fade_n > 0:
 889                ramp = self._ramp[fade_start:fade_end]
 890                stereo_new[:fade_n] = (1.0 - ramp) * stereo_old[:fade_n] + ramp * stereo_new[:fade_n]
 891                self._cf_pos = fade_end
 892
 893            with self._rotation_lock:
 894                # Do not overwrite a newly started fade from the worker thread.
 895                if self._cf_pos == fade_start:
 896                    self._cf_pos = fade_end
 897
 898                    if self._cf_pos >= self._cf_length:
 899                        self._cf_flag = 0
 900                        self._cf_pos = 0
 901                        fade_finished = True
 902                    else:
 903                        fade_finished = False
 904                else:
 905                    # A newer rotation was published during this audio block.
 906                    # Its fade will begin during the next block.
 907                    fade_finished = False
 908        
 909        else:
 910            self._cf_pos = 0
 911            
 912        # Save the current/new filter tail for the next block.
 913        new_tail = stereo_new[block_size:block_size + sh_length - 1].copy()
 914        old_tail = stereo_old[block_size:block_size + sh_length - 1].copy()
 915        
 916        # extract tails for the next block
 917        self.overlap_buffer[:] = new_tail
 918        
 919        if fade_finished:
 920            # The active decoder is now the new filter. Its history must also
 921            # become the "old" history used at the next rotation transition.
 922            self.overlap_buffer_old[:] = new_tail
 923        else:
 924            # A fade is still active, so retain both independent OLA states.
 925            self.overlap_buffer_old[:] = old_tail
 926                
 927        return stereo_new[:block_size]
 928        
 929
 930    def flush(self) -> np.ndarray:
 931        """
 932        Retrieve final tail samples after processing the last audio chunk.
 933        
 934        Returns the remaining M-1 samples (where M is the IR length) stored
 935        in the overlap buffer, which must be output to complete the stream.
 936
 937        Returns
 938        -------
 939        np.ndarray
 940            Tail of the last convolution result with shape (IR_length-1, 2).
 941        """
 942        return self.overlap_buffer.copy()
 943
 944    # updates our hrirs_nm_fft by zero-padding the time signal so the resulting fft has the correct length for convolution
 945    # with ambisonics audio
 946    def update_hrirs_fft(self, block_size: int):
 947        """
 948        Compute and store FFTs of the spherical-harmonic HRIRs zero-padded to block_size.
 949        Additionally, recalculates the current rotation matrix to fit the necessary size
 950        
 951        Parameters
 952        ----------------
 953        block_size : int
 954            FFT length used for convolution; HRIRs are zero-padded to this length.
 955        """
 956        self.hrir_nm_fft = np.fft.fft(self.hrir_nm, n=block_size, axis=-1)
 957        self._apply_rotation()
 958
 959    def close(self):
 960        """
 961        Clean up and terminate the rotation worker thread.
 962        
 963        Sets stop and update flags, joins the rotation thread with a 1-second
 964        timeout, and prints a warning if the thread does not terminate cleanly.
 965        Call this before destroying the SphericalHarmonics instance.
 966
 967        Notes
 968        -----
 969        - Thread join timeout is 1.0 second
 970        - Safe to call multiple times
 971        """
 972        self._stop_rotation_thread.set()
 973        self._rotation_update.set()
 974
 975        # terminate the rotation_thread
 976        if self._rotation_thread is not None:
 977            self._rotation_thread.join(timeout=1.0)
 978
 979            # debug message if processing_thread didn't terminate properly
 980            if self._rotation_thread.is_alive():
 981                print("Warning: Rotation thread did not terminate cleanly.")
 982    
 983    # test if  the channels are clipping
 984    def test_clipping(self, channels):
 985        """
 986        Check provided channels for clipping and print a warning if detected.
 987        The function checks whether any
 988        sample reaches or exceeds the amplitude threshold of 1.0 and
 989        prints a warning message if clipping is found. This function has
 990        no return value and only produces a console side-effect.
 991
 992        Parameters
 993        ----------
 994        channels : sequence of array_like
 995            Iterable of 1-D arrays containing time-domain samples for each
 996            channel (e.g., left and right). 
 997
 998        Notes
 999        ----------------
1000        This function only prints a warning and does not modify data.
1001        """
1002
1003        for channel in channels:
1004            # test for clipping
1005            if np.max(channel) >= 1:
1006                print("\n####################\n" \
1007                "WARNING! WARNING!\n" \
1008                f"Clipping detected!\n" \
1009                "####################")
1010
1011    def set_atol(self, atol):
1012        """
1013        Sets the tolerance for which we accept rotation updates. Default tolerance is 2°.
1014
1015        Parameters
1016        ----------
1017        atol : int
1018            The tolerance in degrees.
1019        """
1020        self.atol = np.deg2rad(atol)
1021
1022    def _set_crossfade_length(self, length: int) -> None:
1023        """
1024        Configure the sample-accurate equal-power crossfade ramp length.
1025        
1026        Creates an equal-power sine-squared ramp (starting at 0, ending at 1)
1027        of the specified sample length. The ramp is independent of audio block
1028        size and used for smooth transitions during head rotations.
1029
1030        Parameters
1031        ----------
1032        length : int
1033            Crossfade duration in samples (must be >= 2).
1034
1035        Raises
1036        ------
1037        ValueError
1038            If length < 2.
1039
1040        Notes
1041        -----
1042        - Ramp phase: sin²(phase) where phase ∈ [0, π/2]
1043        - Equal-power property ensures constant total energy during fade
1044        - Stored in self._ramp and used by process_ola_rot()
1045        """
1046        if length < 2:
1047            raise ValueError("Crossfade length must be at least two samples.")
1048
1049        self._cf_length = int(length)
1050        phase = np.linspace(0.0, np.pi / 2.0, self._cf_length)
1051        self._ramp = np.sin(phase) ** 2
1052        self._cf_pos = 0

Real-time binaural renderer using spherical-harmonic HRTF decomposition.

This class manages the complete pipeline for head-tracked binaural audio: loads an HRTF dataset, decomposes HRIRs into spherical-harmonic coefficients, performs head-rotation transformations via Wigner-D matrices, and applies fast frequency-domain convolution with overlap-add buffering and smooth crossfading during rotation transitions.

Parameters
  • hrtf (HRTF or None, optional): Preloaded HRTF instance. If None, the default FABIAN HRTF is loaded. Default is None.
  • sampling_rate (int or float, optional): Target sampling rate in Hz. HRTF resampling is automatic if needed. Default is 44100.
  • ambi_order (int, optional): Ambisonic order (0–7) for spherical-harmonic decomposition. Default is 1 (first-order).
  • preprocess (str, optional): Preprocessing algorithm: 'LS' (Least Squares), 'MagLS' (recommended), 'TA', or 'BiMagLS'. Default is 'MagLS'.
  • block_size (int, optional): Audio block size in samples. If None, auto-set to next power of two greater than IR length. Default is None.
Attributes
  • hrtf (HRTF): Loaded HRTF dataset instance.
  • sampling_rate (int): Current sampling rate in Hz.
  • ambi_order (int): Current Ambisonic order.
  • sources (spharpy.SamplingSphere): HRTF spatial sampling grid.
  • hrir_nm (np.ndarray): Spherical-harmonic HRIR coefficients (time domain). Shape: (2, n_sh_channels, n_samples).
  • hrir_nm_fft (np.ndarray): Zero-padded FFT of spherical-harmonic HRIRs for convolution. Shape: (2, n_sh_channels, n_freq_bins).
  • hrir_nm_rot (dict): Current and previous rotated SH-HRIR spectra with keys 'old' and 'new'.
  • block_size (int): Audio processing block size in samples.
  • N (int): FFT length for overlap-add (>= block_size + IR_length - 1).
  • overlap_buffer (np.ndarray): Tail from last block for overlap-add continuity. Shape: (IR_length-1, 2).
  • overlap_buffer_old (np.ndarray): Tail from previous rotation filter during crossfade.
  • pre_gain (float): Output gain multiplier (default 0.1).
  • atol (float): Rotation tolerance in radians for skipping negligible updates (default ≈ 1°).
Notes
  • A daemon thread manages asynchronous rotation updates (see _rotation_worker)
  • Uses SN3D normalization and real spherical harmonics (AmbiX convention)
  • Crossfade ramp: 32-sample equal-power sine² curve
  • Call close() before object destruction to cleanly terminate the rotation thread
  • Thread-safe rotation updates via queue and locks
  • Supports smooth head-rotation transitions with zero audio clicks
Examples
>>> sh = SphericalHarmonics(ambi_order=3, sampling_rate=48000)
>>> for chunk in ambi_stream:
...     sh.set_rotation([yaw, pitch, roll])  # Non-blocking queue
...     output = sh.process_ola_rot(chunk)
...     play(output)
>>> sh.close()
SphericalHarmonics( hrtf: HRTF = None, sampling_rate=44100, ambi_order=1, preprocess='MagLS', block_size=None) 
 98    def __init__(self, hrtf: HRTF = None, sampling_rate=44_100, ambi_order=1, preprocess='MagLS', block_size=None):
 99        """
100        Initialize spherical-harmonic HRTF processing and convolution engine.
101        
102        This constructor loads or receives an HRTF dataset, converts HRIRs to
103        spherical-harmonic coefficients for the given Ambisonic order, and
104        initializes the real-time convolution pipeline with overlap-add buffers,
105        rotation matrices, and a background rotation worker thread. This call is
106        blocking and may take considerable time (typically several seconds).
107
108        Parameters
109        ----------
110        hrtf : HRTF or None, optional
111            Preloaded HRTF instance. If None, the default FABIAN HRTF dataset
112            is downloaded and loaded. Default is None.
113        sampling_rate : int or float, optional
114            Target sampling rate in Hz for HRIR resampling. The HRTF will be
115            resampled if its native sampling rate differs. Default is 44100.
116        ambi_order : int, optional
117            Ambisonic order (0, 1, 2, ..., 7) for spherical-harmonic 
118            decomposition. Higher orders require more computation but provide
119            better directional accuracy. Default is 1 (first-order Ambisonics).
120        preprocess : str, optional
121            Preprocessing algorithm for HRTF conversion. Currently supported:
122            'LS' (Least Squares), 'MagLS' (Magnitude Least Squares, recommended),
123            'TA' (not yet implemented), 'BiMagLS' (not yet implemented).
124            Default is 'MagLS'.
125        block_size : int, optional
126            Audio processing block size in samples. Must match the buffer size
127            used in real-time playback for correct overlap-add convolution.
128            If None, automatically set to the next power of two greater than
129            the HRIR length. Default is None.
130
131        Attributes
132        ----------
133        hrtf : HRTF
134            Loaded HRTF instance.
135        sampling_rate : int
136            Current sampling rate in Hz.
137        ambi_order : int
138            Current Ambisonic order.
139        sources : spharpy.SamplingSphere
140            Spatial sampling points of the HRTF measurement directions.
141        hrir_nm : np.ndarray
142            Spherical-harmonic coefficients of HRIRs in time domain.
143        hrir_nm_fft : np.ndarray
144            FFT of zero-padded spherical-harmonic HRIRs (for convolution).
145        hrir_nm_rot : dict
146            Current rotated SH-HRIRs in frequency domain with keys 'old' and 'new'.
147        block_size : int
148            Audio processing block size in samples.
149        N : int
150            FFT length for overlap-add (>= block_size + IR_length - 1).
151        overlap_buffer : np.ndarray
152            Tail samples from last convolution (shape: (IR_length-1, 2)).
153        overlap_buffer_old : np.ndarray
154            Tail samples from previous rotation filter state.
155        pre_gain : float
156            Overall gain factor applied to all output (default 0.1).
157
158        Raises
159        ------
160        Exception
161            If HRTF loading (from file and web) both fail.
162
163        Notes
164        -----
165        - A daemon thread (_rotation_worker) is started for asynchronous head
166        rotation updates; terminate via close() before object destruction
167        - Uses SN3D normalization and real spherical harmonics (AmbiX convention)
168        - Crossfade ramp length is fixed at 32 samples by default
169        - Default tolerance for rotation changes: 1 degree (radians)
170        - Equal-power sine-squared ramps ensure smooth audio during transitions
171        """
172        start = time.time()
173        
174        # # set the hrtf. this should be a pyfar signal!
175        # self.hrtf = hrtf
176
177        # set sample rate. we should make sure this is the same as for the HRTFs!!!
178        self.sampling_rate = sampling_rate
179
180        if hrtf == None:
181            # load FABIAN from the web if no HRTF was given
182            self.hrtf = HRTF()
183        else:
184            self.hrtf = hrtf
185
186        # make sure the sampling rate is correct and resample if necessary
187        if self.hrtf.fs != sampling_rate:
188            self.hrtf.resample(sampling_rate)
189
190        # store the sources in a Sampling Sphere
191        self.sources = sh.SamplingSphere.from_coordinates(self.hrtf.sources)
192
193        # create a spherical harmonics definition, corresponding to the AmbiX convention
194        self.ambi_order = ambi_order
195        self.sh_definition = sh.SphericalHarmonicDefinition(self.ambi_order, 
196                                                            normalization="SN3D", 
197                                                            basis_type='real', 
198                                                            condon_shortley=False
199                                                            )
200
201        # create the spherical harmonics object from definition and sampling sphere
202        self.spherical_harmonics = sh.SphericalHarmonics.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
203                                                                         self.sources, 
204                                                                        #  inverse_method="pseudo_inverse"
205                                                                         )
206
207        # create hrtf processing unit
208        self.process = Processing()
209
210        # create h_nm matrix 
211        hrirs_nm = self.process.apply_preprocessing(self.hrtf.hrirs, 
212                                               self.spherical_harmonics,
213                                               algorithm=preprocess
214                                               )
215        
216        print("Convert to Spherical Harmonic Signal")
217        self.hrir_nm = sh.SphericalHarmonicSignal.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
218                                                                   hrirs_nm.time, 
219                                                                   hrirs_nm.sampling_rate
220                                                                   ).time
221        
222        *_, pad_to_length = self.hrir_nm.shape
223
224        # update this later by calling update_hrirs_fft() once we know the desired fft length
225        self.hrir_nm_fft = np.fft.fft(self.hrir_nm, next_power_of_two(pad_to_length), axis=-1)
226
227        # create SH rotation unit
228        self.rotation = RotationMatrix()
229        # prepare rotated hrir's, and our rotation matrix, with all angles 0 currently
230        self.hrir_nm_rot = {
231                           'old' : self.hrir_nm_fft.copy(),
232                           'new' : self.hrir_nm_fft.copy()
233                           }
234        self._D = {
235                  'old' : np.eye(order_to_channel_n(ambi_order)),
236                  'new' : np.eye(order_to_channel_n(ambi_order))
237                  }
238        self._last_rotation = Rotation.from_euler('zyx', (0, 0, 0))
239        self.atol = np.deg2rad(1)
240
241        self._rotation_lock = threading.Lock()
242        self._rotation_queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=1)
243        self._rotation_update = threading.Event()
244        self._stop_rotation_thread = threading.Event()
245
246        # start the rotation thread
247        self._rotation_thread = threading.Thread(
248            target=self._rotation_worker,
249            daemon=True,
250        )
251        self._rotation_thread.start()
252
253        # States for overlap-add (must be reset on seek)
254        self.overlap_buffer = np.zeros((self.get_IR_length() - 1, 2), dtype=np.float32)
255        self.overlap_buffer_old = np.zeros_like(self.overlap_buffer)
256        self.interpolate_rot = None
257        # overlap add L = self.get_IR_length()
258        if block_size is None:
259            block_size = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length())
260        self.block_size = block_size
261        # overlap add N
262        # compute N >= M + L - 1
263        self.N = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length() + block_size - 1)
264
265        # prepare ramp for crossfading between rotations
266        self._cf_flag = 0
267        self._set_crossfade_length(32)
268
269        # use this function because we will not calculate D otherwise
270        self.update_rotation_matrix([0, 0, 0])
271
272        # prepare pre_gain for gianstaging
273        self.pre_gain = 0.1
274        print(f"Setting up Spherical Harmonics took {time.time() - start:.2f}s")

Initialize spherical-harmonic HRTF processing and convolution engine.

This constructor loads or receives an HRTF dataset, converts HRIRs to spherical-harmonic coefficients for the given Ambisonic order, and initializes the real-time convolution pipeline with overlap-add buffers, rotation matrices, and a background rotation worker thread. This call is blocking and may take considerable time (typically several seconds).

Parameters
  • hrtf (HRTF or None, optional): Preloaded HRTF instance. If None, the default FABIAN HRTF dataset is downloaded and loaded. Default is None.
  • sampling_rate (int or float, optional): Target sampling rate in Hz for HRIR resampling. The HRTF will be resampled if its native sampling rate differs. Default is 44100.
  • ambi_order (int, optional): Ambisonic order (0, 1, 2, ..., 7) for spherical-harmonic decomposition. Higher orders require more computation but provide better directional accuracy. Default is 1 (first-order Ambisonics).
  • preprocess (str, optional): Preprocessing algorithm for HRTF conversion. Currently supported: 'LS' (Least Squares), 'MagLS' (Magnitude Least Squares, recommended), 'TA' (not yet implemented), 'BiMagLS' (not yet implemented). Default is 'MagLS'.
  • block_size (int, optional): Audio processing block size in samples. Must match the buffer size used in real-time playback for correct overlap-add convolution. If None, automatically set to the next power of two greater than the HRIR length. Default is None.
Attributes
  • hrtf (HRTF): Loaded HRTF instance.
  • sampling_rate (int): Current sampling rate in Hz.
  • ambi_order (int): Current Ambisonic order.
  • sources (spharpy.SamplingSphere): Spatial sampling points of the HRTF measurement directions.
  • hrir_nm (np.ndarray): Spherical-harmonic coefficients of HRIRs in time domain.
  • hrir_nm_fft (np.ndarray): FFT of zero-padded spherical-harmonic HRIRs (for convolution).
  • hrir_nm_rot (dict): Current rotated SH-HRIRs in frequency domain with keys 'old' and 'new'.
  • block_size (int): Audio processing block size in samples.
  • N (int): FFT length for overlap-add (>= block_size + IR_length - 1).
  • overlap_buffer (np.ndarray): Tail samples from last convolution (shape: (IR_length-1, 2)).
  • overlap_buffer_old (np.ndarray): Tail samples from previous rotation filter state.
  • pre_gain (float): Overall gain factor applied to all output (default 0.1).
Raises
  • Exception: If HRTF loading (from file and web) both fail.
Notes
  • A daemon thread (_rotation_worker) is started for asynchronous head rotation updates; terminate via close() before object destruction
  • Uses SN3D normalization and real spherical harmonics (AmbiX convention)
  • Crossfade ramp length is fixed at 32 samples by default
  • Default tolerance for rotation changes: 1 degree (radians)
  • Equal-power sine-squared ramps ensure smooth audio during transitions

def update_order(self, order: int, block_size=None): 
276    def update_order(self, order: int, block_size=None):
277        """
278        Update the Ambisonic order and recompute all spherical-harmonic components.
279        
280        This method recalculates the spherical-harmonic basis, performs preprocessing
281        on the HRIRs for the new order, and updates all internal FFT buffers and 
282        rotation matrices. This call is blocking and may take considerable time.
283
284        Parameters
285        ----------
286        order : int
287            New Ambisonic order for spherical-harmonic decomposition.
288        block_size : int, optional
289            Audio processing block size in samples. If None, automatically computed 
290            as the next power of two greater than IR length. Default is None.
291
292        Raises
293        ------
294        ValueError
295            If order is negative.
296        """
297        # create a spherical harmonics definition, corresponding to the AmbiX convention
298        self.ambi_order = order
299        self.sh_definition = sh.SphericalHarmonicDefinition(self.ambi_order, 
300                                                            normalization="SN3D", 
301                                                            basis_type='real', 
302                                                            condon_shortley=False
303                                                            )
304
305        # create the spherical harmonics object from definition and sampling sphere
306        self.spherical_harmonics = sh.SphericalHarmonics.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
307                                                                         self.sources, 
308                                                                         inverse_method="pseudo_inverse"
309                                                                         )
310        # create h_nm matrix 
311        hrirs_nm = self.process.apply_preprocessing(self.hrtf.hrirs, 
312                                               self.spherical_harmonics,
313                                               algorithm='MagLS'
314                                               )
315        
316        # update our hrir_nm
317        self.hrir_nm = sh.SphericalHarmonicSignal.from_definition(self.sh_definition, 
318                                                                   hrirs_nm.time, 
319                                                                   hrirs_nm.sampling_rate
320                                                                   ).time
321        
322        # prepare hrir_nm_fft
323        if block_size is None:
324            block_size = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length())
325        # this calls update_hrirs_fft internally!
326        self.update_process_variables(block_size)

329    def update_process_variables(self, block_size: int):
330        """
331        Updated the variables necessary to perform successfull Overlap-Add algorithm on processing.
332
333        Parameters
334        ----------
335        block_size : int
336            The buffer size we are currently working with
337        """
338        self.block_size = block_size
339        # compute N >= M + L - 1
340        self.N = next_power_of_two(self.get_IR_length() + block_size - 1)
341
342        # update our sh fft coefficients once (and on each rotation update)
343        self.update_hrirs_fft(self.N)

346        self._set_crossfade_length(32)

349        self.overlap_buffer = np.zeros((self.get_IR_length() - 1, 2), dtype=np.float32)
350        self.overlap_buffer_old = np.zeros_like(self.overlap_buffer)

def restart_rotation(self): 
364    def restart_rotation(self):
365        """
366        Terminate the current rotation thread and start a new one.
367        
368        This method safely closes any existing rotation worker thread, clears
369        synchronization flags, and spawns a fresh daemon thread. Use this after
370        major configuration changes or when rotation state needs to be reset.
371
372        Raises
373        ------
374        Exception
375            If the existing rotation thread cannot be terminated within 1 second.
376        """
377        # close old rotation thread if it exists and is alive
378        if self._rotation_thread is not None:
379            if self._rotation_thread.is_alive():
380                # set the stop flag, set rotation update and hope old thread will close
381                self._stop_rotation_thread.set()
382                self._rotation_update.set()
383                self._rotation_thread.join(1.)
384                if self._rotation_thread.is_alive():
385                    raise Exception("Couldn't close rotation thread.")
386                
387            self._rotation_thread = None
388
389        # clear the stop and rotation flag
390        self._stop_rotation_thread.clear()
391        self._rotation_update.clear()
392        # start a new rotation thread
393        self._rotation_thread = threading.Thread(
394            target=self._rotation_worker,
395            daemon=True,
396        )
397        self._rotation_thread.start()

def update_rotation_matrix(self, angles, convention='zyx'): 
399    def update_rotation_matrix(self, angles, convention='zyx'):
400        """
401        Directly Compute and update the internal Wigner-D matrix based on thie given Euler angles in degrees (zyx). This will block the thread!
402        The updating is done in a thread-safe manner.
403
404        Parameters
405        ----------
406        angles : sequence of float
407            Euler angles in degrees as (z, y, x).
408        convention : str
409            A string identifying the used convention/order of the angles. 'zyx' is default.
410        """
411        rotation = Rotation.from_euler(convention, angles, degrees=True)
412        alpha, beta, gamma = rotation.as_euler("zyz")
413        new_D = self.rotation.real_wigner_d_matrix(self.ambi_order, alpha, beta, gamma)
414
415         # using the fft, since we expect this to be faster than time domain
416        # 3. Apply rotation
417        # data is (Channels, SH, Time/Freq)
418        # D is (SH, SH)
419        # We want D @ data
420        # einsum: ij, cjk -> cik
421        # self.hrir_nm_rot = np.einsum("ij, cjk -> cik", self.D, hrir_rot)
422        new_rot = new_D @ self.hrir_nm_fft
423        with self._rotation_lock:
424            self._D['old'] = self._D['new'].copy()
425            self._D['new'] = new_D
426            self.hrir_nm_rot['old'] = self.hrir_nm_rot['new'].copy()
427            self.hrir_nm_rot['new'] = new_rot
428
429            # also swap old OLA buffer. new one gets updated in OLA logic
430            # self.overlap_buffer_old = self.overlap_buffer.copy()
431            # self.overlap_buffer[:] = 0.0
432
433            # a crossfade needs to happen now!
434            self._cf_flag = 1
435            self._cf_pos = 0

def set_rotation(self, angles, convention='zyx'): 
437    def set_rotation(self, angles, convention='zyx'):
438        """
439        Compute and update the internal Wigner-D matrix based on thie given Euler angles in degrees (zyx) by passing it to the worker thread.
440        The updating is done in a thread-safe manner.
441
442        Parameters
443        ----------
444        angles : sequence of float
445            Euler angles in degrees as (z, y, x).
446        convention : str
447            A string identifying the used convention/order of the angles. 'zyx' is default.
448        """
449        try:
450            self._rotation_queue.put_nowait((angles, convention))
451        except queue.Full:
452            try:
453                # drop the last cached block. queue should be empty now, since we only have size 1
454                self._rotation_queue.get_nowait()
455                print("Queue is already full! Dropping this rotation update")
456            except queue.Empty:
457                pass
458            # try putting a new block into the queue again after draining it
459            self._rotation_queue.put_nowait((angles, convention))
460
461        # finally, set the flag if we managed to successfully set a rotation
462        self._rotation_update.set()
